item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
India highlights major expansion of medical, nursing and allied healthcare workforce; reaffirms commitment to equitable access to specialized care for rural, tribal and underserved populations at WHO RC79
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Addresses Ministerial Roundtable at 79th WHO Regional Committee Session
Medical Colleges More Than Double Since 2014; MBBS and PG Seats Rise by Over 175%: Shri J.P. Nadda
WHO South-East Asia Region Adopts Dili Declaration on Equity in Specialized Care
WHO Recognises India’s Sustained Leadership in Maternal Health and Noncommunicable Disease Management; honoured with Two WHO South-East Asia Regional Awards
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, participated in the Ministerial Roundtable on “Human Resources for Health: Equity in Specialized Care” held during the 79th Session of the WHO Regional Committee for South-East Asia (RC79) in Timor-Leste. The Roundtable brought together Health Ministers and senior representatives of Member States of the WHO South-East Asia Region to deliberate on strengthening health workforce capacity and ensuring equitable access to specialized healthcare.

Addressing the Roundtable, Shri J.P. Nadda emphasized that equitable access to specialized care is integral to achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and requires a comprehensive approach encompassing education and training, deployment, retention and continuing professional development of the healthcare workforce.

The Union Health Minister highlighted India's significant progress in expanding its health workforce capacity and strengthening access to specialized healthcare, particularly for people living in rural, tribal, underserved and hard-to-reach areas.

Shri Nadda highlighted that the Government of India has significantly expanded medical education infrastructure through the establishment of new medical colleges and upgradation of existing Government Medical Colleges, resulting in a substantial increase in undergraduate and postgraduate medical seats.

Since 2014, the number of medical colleges in the country has more than doubled from 387 to 858, registering an increase of 121.71 per cent. During the same period, MBBS seats have increased from 51,348 to 1,42,464, an increase of 177.45 per cent, while postgraduate seats have risen from 31,185 to 86,287, an increase of 176.69 per cent.

The Minister also highlighted the targeted expansion of postgraduate capacity. The schemes for increasing medical seats were extended in September 2025, with a target of creating 10,000 additional postgraduate seats by 2028–29, with priority accorded to underserved areas and shortage specialities such as Emergency Medicine, Geriatrics, Psychiatry and Family Medicine.

Highlighting the importance of a strong and diversified healthcare workforce, Shri Nadda stated that 157 new nursing colleges are being established co-located with existing medical colleges. These institutions are expected to add approximately 15,700 nursing graduates annually, with particular emphasis on improving access to quality and affordable nursing education in underserved districts and States/Union Territories.

He further noted that Nurse Practitioner Programmes have been introduced in 10 critical specialities, supported by the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Act, 2023.

The Union Minister also highlighted India's efforts to expand the allied and healthcare workforce. The Government has announced the creation of 1,00,000 allied and healthcare professionals over five years, supported by the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021 and the establishment of the National Commission in 2024. The Commission brings 57 diverse allied and healthcare professions within a structured regulatory framework.

Shri Nadda highlighted the role of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in providing comprehensive primary healthcare, including screening, early identification and referral services. Ayushman Arogya Shivirs further extend screening and specialist consultations to underserved communities.

He also highlighted the role of Community Health Centres and First Referral Units in providing specialist and referral services. To improve the availability and retention of specialists in difficult areas, India is adopting flexible mechanisms including competitive remuneration, difficult-area allowances, in-sourcing of speciality services, performance-based incentives and fixed-tenure postings.

The Union Minister emphasized that India is leveraging digital health technologies to overcome geographical barriers and extend access to specialist services. Platforms such as eSanjeevani and ABHA-enabled digital health records are facilitating teleconsultation, referrals and continuity of care, particularly for populations in remote and underserved areas.

Shri Nadda underscored that India's approach is moving towards building a larger, more diverse and geographically well-distributed health workforce, with sustained emphasis on underserved areas and shortage specialities. He highlighted that these measures reflect a team-based and continuum-of-care approach to advancing equity in specialized care.

A key outcome of RC79 was the adoption of the “Dili Declaration on Human Resources for Health: Equity in Specialized Care” by the Health Ministers of Member States of the WHO South-East Asia Region.

Through the Declaration, Member States have committed to a comprehensive set of actions aimed at addressing health workforce shortages, maldistribution and the growing need for specialized healthcare.

The Declaration calls for aligning health workforce planning, education and financing with current and future demographic, epidemiological and health emergency preparedness needs. It also calls for policies to attract, recruit, deploy, retain and improve the performance of specialist health workers, particularly in rural and underserved areas, guided by the WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel.

The Declaration further emphasizes optimizing the existing workforce through task-sharing, mentoring, rotational outreach and visiting specialist programmes, including collaboration with qualified and registered Traditional, Complementary and Integrated Medicine practitioners.

Member States have also committed to strengthening integrated referral systems and continuity of care through primary healthcare teams, specialist outreach services, teleconsultation networks and coordinated referral hospitals.

The Declaration calls for strengthening public health workforce capacity and essential public health functions, while accelerating the safe and equitable adoption of digital health technologies, including telemedicine, teleconsultation and AI-supported clinical tools, to expand access to specialist services for rural, remote and underserved populations.

It further promotes innovative service delivery models, including mobile and outreach specialist teams and community-based specialist care, with integration of Traditional, Complementary and Integrated Medicine services.

The Member States also agreed to integrate palliative care into health systems at all levels through workforce development, multidisciplinary teams, community-based services and strengthened referral pathways.

The Declaration emphasizes strengthening national capacity for high-priority specialized services, including cancer, cardiovascular care, trauma, maternal and newborn care, mental health, geriatric care and rehabilitative care. It also calls for strengthening national health workforce information systems to support evidence-based policy-making.

Recognizing the importance of regional cooperation, Member States committed to facilitating information exchange, joint training, clinical mentorship and regional collaboration, including through a regional network of health professional regulators and policy-makers.

The Dili Declaration recalls the commitments made under the 2023 Delhi Declaration on strengthening primary healthcare and responds to the Region's rapid demographic and epidemiological transition, rising burden of complex and chronic conditions, and persistent shortages and maldistribution of specialist health workers.

Member States called upon the World Health Organization to support implementation of the commitments through technical assistance, capacity-building, policy guidance and strengthened regional collaboration mechanisms.

India welcomed the adoption of the Dili Declaration as a significant step towards ensuring equitable access to specialized care, advancing Universal Health Coverage and realizing Health for All across the South-East Asia Region. India reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with Member States and the WHO to translate the commitments of the Declaration into concrete action.

Furthermore, at the 79th Session of the WHO Regional Committee, India was honoured with two WHO South-East Asia Regional awards, recognising the country's sustained achievements in critical areas of public health.

India received recognition for Sustaining the regional elimination of maternal and neonatal tetanus over the past decade; and Strong leadership in addressing noncommunicable diseases through primary healthcare, including achievement of national targets for placing people on protocol-based management for hypertension and diabetes.

The recognition reflects India's sustained commitment to strengthening primary healthcare, disease prevention, early detection and effective management of priority health conditions.

The Union Health Minister dedicated these recognitions to the frontline health workers across the country, whose unwavering commitment and dedicated service have been instrumental in strengthening India's health system and contributing to improved health outcomes.

The Government of India remains committed to advancing Universal Health Coverage through investments in health infrastructure, human resources, primary healthcare, digital health and health system resilience.

*****

SR

Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), organized the STPI Electropreneur Summit 2026 at IIIT-Delhi. The summit brought together government leadership, academic pioneers, and industry stalwarts to deliberate on expanding India’s Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) footprint.

A key highlight of the event was the launch of the Open Challenge Programme of the STPI Electropreneur Park. The programme seeks to identify and support innovative technology solutions and startups in the ESDM domain. On the occasion, MoUs were exchanged between AIC STPINEXT INITIATIVES and Spoke Centres (11 partner institutions spanning Chandigarh, Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and Uttarakhand) as well as investors (Indian Angel Network Services Private Limited (IAN) & Solara VC), to strengthen collaboration and expand the reach of the Electropreneur ecosystem. The EP 2.0 Spoke Centres, which will democratize access to ESDM incubation and enable innovators across the region to access incubation, mentoring, infrastructure and ecosystem support, include ACIC RISE, Association Chandigarh; Engineering College, CEC Landran; NSUT Incubation and Innovation Foundation (NSUT-IIF); KR Mangalam Incubation & Entrepreneurship Centre (KEIC Foundation); Manav Rachna University, Faridabad; IIT Mandi Catalyst; NewGen IEDC–Business and Innovation Centre, University of Kashmir; MNIT Innovation and Incubation Centre (MIIC), MNIT Jaipur; AKGEC Skills Foundation; Sharda Launchpad Federation, Sharda University, Greater Noida; Swami Rama Himalayan University, Dehradun; UPES Council for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (UCIE); and Runway Incubator.

The inaugural session commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp following welcome remarks by Mrs. Vandana Srivastava, Director, STPI-Noida. Prominent ecosystem leaders delivered opening addresses, including Shri Pradeep Gupta, CMD of CyberMedia; Shri Ashok Chandak, President of IESA & SEMI India; and Prof. Sandeep Sen, Director of IIIT-Delhi. 

Delivering the Special Address, Shri K.K. Singh, Joint Secretary, MeitY, highlighted the importance of innovation and entrepreneurship in advancing India’s ESDM ecosystem and spoke about the initiatives being undertaken by the Ministry to support growth in the sector. He said, “India's technology journey is entering a crucial next stage combining our proven global leadership in software with an aggressive push toward Electronic System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) and semiconductors. EP 1.0 laid a strong foundation, nurturing 59 startups, filing 66 patents, and creating over ₹640 crore in startup valuation. With EP 2.0, we are scaling our ambitions to target 500 startups, expanding deep into Tier-II and Tier-III cities so that talent across every corner of the nation can participate in this growth. Our true benchmark for success will be converting this immense talent into commercialized intellectual property and globally competitive products.”

Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, in his special address highlighted the objectives of the STPI Electropreneur Summit and the significant transformation in India’s technology and electronics landscape and the growing opportunities for innovators in Deep Tech, AI and Electronic System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM). He said, “Today marks an exciting time for technology in India. Historically, our talent shifted primarily toward software services building a $200B+ export industry while electronics manufacturing lagged. But the landscape has fundamentally changed. Over the past decade, national electronics production grew seven times from under ₹2 lakh crore to over ₹13 lakh crore, while exports surged eleven times to ₹4.24 lakh crore. Speaking about Electropreneur Park, he highlighted its journey and the progress achieved through EP 1.0, which has delivered 129 products, 27 trademarks, 66 patent filings and ₹150 crore in cumulative revenue. Now, with Electropreneur Park 2.0, we are taking this vision to the next level from nurturing 500 startups to building a strong and interconnected ESDM innovation ecosystem across North India. Further, with various other government initiatives i.e. GPU access through the India AI Mission, and the ₹1.275 lakh crore through ISM 2.0 scheme, this is the right time for young innovators to build hardware, design products, and lead global electronics manufacturing.

The afternoon program featured a technical address by Shri S.K. Marwah, Advisor, R&D Electronics Division, MeitY. This set the stage for a panel discussion on "Bridging the Gap: Accelerating ESDM Innovation through Government-Academia-Industry Synergies," moderated by Dr. Anuj Grover, Associate Professor at IIIT-Delhi, along with other panelists Dr. Amjad Hussain, Director - HCIE, SRHU – Dehradun, Shri Rajoo Goel, Secretary General, ELCINA, Shri S.K Marwah, Advisor, R&D Electronics Division, MeitY.

The STPI Electropreneur Summit is a premier initiative by STPI that brings together Electropreneurs, innovators, startups, industry leaders, investors, academia and policymakers to exchange ideas, forge partnerships, unlock opportunities and shape the future of electronics and deep-tech innovation in India. An electropreneur is an entrepreneur who starts, develops, and scales businesses specifically within the electronics and hardware-driven technology sectors.

During the Summit, the Open Challenge Programme (OCP) for the STPI Electropreneur Park was launched, along with the exchange of MoUs with 11 Spoke Centres as well as with investors, including Indian Angel Network Services Private Limited (IAN) and Solara VC.

The Spoke Centres of STPI Electropreneur Park CoE, New Delhi, are partner institutions spanning Chandigarh, Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand that will facilitate extending the reach of the Electropreneur Park and provide incubation support, mentorship, infrastructure and ecosystem access to innovators and startups in their respective regions.

About STPI:

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organization under Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) engaged in promoting IT/ITES Industry, innovation, R&D, start-ups, product/IP creation in the field of emerging technologies like IoT, Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Computer Vision, Robotics, Robotics Process Automation (RPA), Augmented & Virtual Reality, Animation & Visual effect, Data Science & Analytics for various domains like Gaming, FinTech, Agritech, MedTech, Autonomous Connected Electric & Shared(ACES) Mobility, ESDM, Cyber Security, Industry 4.0, Drone, Efficiency Augmentation, etc.

Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
MoSJE Expands Partnerships with Spiritual Organisations under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
MoUs with Four Spiritual Organisations to be Signed Tomorrow in New Delhi
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, is expanding its collaboration with spiritual organisations under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), advancing the shared vision of building a drug-free India.

Recognizing the vital role of spiritual organisations in guiding communities, instilling discipline and promoting value-based living, the Department has partnered with leading spiritual institutions to strengthen outreach and awareness against substance abuse.

In continuation of this initiative, the Department will sign MoUs with Adhyatm Vigyan Satsang Kendra, Chinmaya Mission, Divya Jyoti Jagrati Sansthan and Hare Krishna Movement.  The signing ceremony will be held at the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in the National Capital here tomorrow Wednesday, in the presence of Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, senior officials of the Department and revered spiritual gurus.

Earlier, Memoranda of Understanding were signed with The Art of Living, Brahma Kumaris, Sant Nirankari Mission, ISKCON, Shri Ram Chandra Mission, All World Gayatri Pariwar, Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Dhanwantari Ashram and the University of Patanjali.

These partnerships have supported mass-awareness programmes, volunteer mobilisation and the integration of yoga, meditation and spiritual counselling into de-addiction efforts.

as a Nasha Mukti Mitr!

 

The involvement of spiritual organisations provides moral guidance, fosters resilience and helps mobilise communities at the grassroots level. By combining spiritual strength with social mobilisation, NMBA seeks to ensure that the message of prevention and recovery resonates across diverse sections of society.

The Ministry believes that these partnerships will reinforce the collective resolve and whole-of-society approach required to realise the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat, contributing to a healthier, stronger and more resilient nation on its journey towards Viksit Bharat.

item.title: AI Keeps an Eye on the ‘Cattle of the Hills’ — and It Could Change How Farmers Watch Their Herds
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare AI Keeps an Eye on the ‘Cattle of the Hills’ — and It Could Change How Farmers Watch Their Herds At an ICAR farm in Nagaland, cameras and artificial intelligence are learning to read the everyday behaviour of Mithun. The technology could eventually help farmers with breeding, animal health and round-the-clock monitoring. Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi In a significant step towards integrating artificial intelligence with livestock research and management, researchers at the ICAR-National Research Centre on Mithun…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
AI Keeps an Eye on the ‘Cattle of the Hills’ — and It Could Change How Farmers Watch Their Herds
At an ICAR farm in Nagaland, cameras and artificial intelligence are learning to read the everyday behaviour of Mithun. The technology could eventually help farmers with breeding, animal health and round-the-clock monitoring.
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards integrating artificial intelligence with livestock research and management, researchers at the ICAR-National Research Centre on Mithun (ICAR-NRC on Mithun), Nagaland, have developed an artificial intelligence-based system for real-time detection and tracking of Mithun behaviour in a natural farm environment. The research has the potential to support continuous monitoring of animal behaviour and provide valuable inputs for animal health, welfare, breeding and reproductive management.

The study, recently published in Engineering Research Express, presents an AI-based, real-time and non-contact framework for the automatic detection and tracking of Mithun (Bos frontalis) behaviour. Mithun, popularly known as the “Cattle of the Hills”, holds significant social, cultural and economic importance for tribal communities across Northeast India and contributes to livelihoods and food security in the region.

Monitoring livestock behaviour is an important component of animal management, as changes in feeding, standing, lying and reproductive behaviour can provide early indications regarding an animal's health, comfort, nutrition and physiological condition. However, conventional monitoring depends largely on manual observation, which is labour-intensive and difficult to sustain continuously, particularly during night hours.

To address this challenge, researchers deployed 12 high-definition CCTV cameras across two sheds at the ICAR-NRC on Mithun farm in Nagaland. The cameras provided continuous day-and-night surveillance, including infrared coverage. Using the recorded footage, the research team developed a dataset comprising 3,000 manually annotated images representing four key Mithun behaviours—feeding, standing, lying and mounting.

The AI framework combines the YOLOv8n model for behaviour detection with DeepSORT technology for tracking individual animals across video frames and assigning persistent identities. The system is capable of identifying the behaviour being performed by an animal while simultaneously tracking individual Mithun in real time.

The YOLOv8n model achieved a mean average precision of 99.5 per cent at mAP@0.5, with a recall of 99.6 per cent. The system recorded a processing speed of approximately 31 frames per second on an NVIDIA RTX 3060 graphics processing unit, demonstrating its capability for real-time application. The framework was also tested under challenging farm conditions, including partial occlusion, background clutter, uneven and wet ground, shadows, motion blur and nighttime infrared footage.

The technology has significant potential for improving livestock monitoring and management. Changes in feeding, standing and lying patterns can provide useful insights into an animal's health, comfort and physiological condition, while mounting behaviour can support reproductive and oestrus management. Continuous automated monitoring could enable farmers and livestock managers to access behavioural information without requiring constant physical observation of animals throughout the day and night.

Two behaviours, tracked with unique IDs — lying and feeding detected in one frame at 96% confidence.

Night vision: mounting behaviour caught in infrared at 97% confidence.

 

The researchers noted that the system has currently been evaluated at a single farm and requires further validation across different farms, geographical regions, seasons, stocking densities and camera arrangements. The present study focuses on four behaviours, while severe occlusion can affect detection and tracking performance. Further research is also required for quantitative evaluation of identity tracking using standard tracking metrics.

The researchers envisage expanding the AI framework to identify additional behaviours such as aggression, grooming and disease-related inactivity. Future work may also explore temporal AI models, edge-device deployment and the development of larger datasets covering different farms and seasons.

The study demonstrates the potential of combining livestock science with artificial intelligence and computer vision to develop technology-enabled solutions for livestock management. Such innovations could strengthen precision livestock farming and support farmers through continuous, data-driven monitoring of animal behaviour.

The research was published in Engineering Research Express, Volume 8 (2026), Article 175213. The study was conducted by researchers from ICAR-NRC on Mithun, Nagaland, in collaboration with NIT Nagaland, Nagaland University and CHRIST (Deemed to be University).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Fresh impetus to India-Morocco defence cooperation: Inaugural Joint Defence Committee meeting held in New Delhi
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

The inaugural Joint Defence Committee meeting between India and Morocco took place in New Delhi on September 08, 2026. The two sides discussed areas of mutual interest in the field of training & education, peacekeeping operations, military exercises, medical cooperation, cyber defence and defence industries. They agreed to further expand defence ties as bilateral cooperation is moving towards its 70th anniversary in 2027.

The meeting was co-chaired by Joint Secretary (International Cooperation), Ministry of Defence Shri Amitabh Prasad and Chief of the 2nd Bureau of the Moroccan Royal Armed Forces Brigadier General Abdellah Athmani. The Indian delegation comprised officers from Department of Defence, three Services, HQ Integrated Defence Staff, Department of Defence Production, DG Armed Forces Medical Services, DRDO and Ministry of External Affairs.

The Moroccan delegation is on a visit to India from September 07 to 10, 2026. Brigadier General Abdellah Athmani commenced his visit by paying tribute to the bravehearts at the National War Memorial, New Delhi. The Moroccan delegation also interacted with defence industries at DPSU Bhawan, New Delhi to get first-hand exposure to India’s growing defence manufacturing capabilities. Both sides agreed to explore avenues of cooperation in the field of co-production, joint ventures, technology collaborations, maintenance and sustainment.

The delegation will be visiting Army Hospital (Research & Referral) to get an overview of India’s military medicine capabilities.

An MoU on cooperation in the field of defence between the two countries was signed during the visit of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh to Morocco in September 2025. The visit provided fresh momentum to bilateral defence relations. The JDC meeting is a part of the institutional mechanism set up through the MoU.

item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment National Pledge Against Drug Abuse To Commemorate The 6th Anniversary Of The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan; Grand National Event By the End Of This Month 3rd High Level Coordination Meeting Discusses Plan, Comprehensive Strategy To Ensure Participation Of 10 Crore+ Citizens In Nationwide Pledge In Line With The Objectives Of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan NMBA e-Pledge On https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/epledge Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aims to mobilise 10 Crore+…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National Pledge Against Drug Abuse To Commemorate The 6th Anniversary Of The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan; Grand National Event By the End Of This Month
3rd High Level Coordination Meeting Discusses Plan, Comprehensive Strategy To Ensure Participation Of 10 Crore+ Citizens In Nationwide Pledge In Line With The Objectives Of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
NMBA e-Pledge On https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/epledge
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aims to mobilise 10 Crore+ citizens through both physical and online participation to undertake the National Mass Pledge Against Drug Abuse, scheduled by the end of this month to mark the 6th anniversary of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA).

As part of ongoing preparations, the 3rd high level coordination meeting chaired by Joint Secretary (Drug Prevention) in the Ministry Dr. Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, held in National Capital today, discussed the plan and the comprehensive strategy to ensure the participation of 10 Crore+ citizens in nationwide pledge through physical and online mode in line with the objectives of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan outlined by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Dr Rathod briefed the participants about the importance of adopting ‘Whole of the Govt’ and ‘Whole of The Society’ approach, to mobilize all stakeholders in pursuit of sensitizing the common people about the dangers and challenges posed by the substance abuse profoundly affecting cross section of people, across the country.

The meeting was also attended by Director, DoSJE (DP) Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, Under Secretary Shri Arun Kumar Karn, besides other officials of the Ministry.

The meeting attended by the senior representatives from various ministries and departments, reviewed the ongoing work for the comprehensive implementation strategy. The role of Line Ministries and Departments was discussed and reviewed in mobilising officers, officials, students, parents, volunteers and other stakeholders for the nationwide pledge.

The meeting discussed organizing pledge ceremonies across all affiliated offices, educational institutions, autonomous bodies, PSUs and field formations under respective Ministries and Departments including Railways, Defence, Civil Defence, Youth Affairs & Sports, School & Higher Education, Post, Police, CAPF, NCC, AYUSH, Rural Development, Health & Family Wefare Revenue besides social, voluntary, spiritual organizations and social influencers.

The Uniform Reporting Mechanism for submission of participation details and outreach, was also discussed in the meeting.

A power point presentation on the plan and coordinated strategy, was discussed threadbare which witnessed active deliberations by all the representatives from the Line Departments and the Ministries.

NMBA Pledge is an initiative to volunteer for reaching out to the victims of substance abuse. The pledge aims to encourage responsible behaviour to instil a sense of responsibility among people to stay away from drugs, to promote and foster sense of Unity and Commitment for encouraging stakeholders to work together towards a common goal. The Pledge further seeks to empower youth to contribute actively to developing a drug-free society.

The link of the NMBA e-Pledge is: https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/epledge

The meeting also highlighted to focus on the significant message to promote and encourage Drug De-addiction through Helpline—14446.

The meeting focussed on the evolving spirit among citizens to act as volunteers by registering as Nasha Mukti Mitr through Department’s official website:

https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/nasha-mukti-mitr

The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) on 15th August 2020 to combat drug demand in the country. Recognizing the urgent need for collective action, the Ministry coordinates various initiatives including prevention, assessment, treatment, rehabilitation, aftercare, public information dissemination, and community awareness.

The Ministry is implementing a comprehensive and evidence-based strategy under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR). The strategy is based on the findings of the first National Survey on the Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India conducted by National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC) at AIIMS, New Delhi.

Under NAPDDR, the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments, Union Territories, NGOs and Government hospitals for preventive education, awareness generation, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation.

As on date, the campaign has reached more than 34.42 crore citizens including over 13.64 Crore youth and 10.58 Crore women, through nationwide awareness activities. More than 1.65 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras (NMM) have also joined the campaign to strengthen community participation.

The NMBA Portal is https://www.dosje.gov.in/organisation/nasha-mukt-bharat-abhiyaan/

To improve accessibility to treatment services, the Ministry has launched the NMBA 2.0 Mobile Application enabling citizens to locate the nearest de-addiction centre.

 

The App can be downloaded from the Google Play Store via this Link: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dosje.nmba_app&hl=en_IN

The Government continues to strengthen its commitment towards a drug-free and socially inclusive India by expanding rehabilitation infrastructure, enhancing preventive interventions, simplifying implementation procedures and ensuring efficient delivery of Centrally Sponsored Schemes. Through sustained community participation, improved governance and technology-enabled service delivery, the Ministry remains committed to protecting vulnerable communities and promoting social justice for all.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
CHIEF OF THE NAVAL STAFF ON AN OFFICIAL VISIT TO AUSTRALIA AND NEW ZEALAND
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, will undertake an official visit to Australia and New Zealand commencing 09 Sep 2026. The visit is aimed at further strengthening the Indian Navy’s bilateral cooperation with the Royal Australian Navy (RAN) and the Royal New Zealand Navy (RNZN).

The visit to Australia builds upon the growing momentum in India–Australia relations, following the Third India-Australia Annual Summit held in Jul 2026 and the Second India–Australia Defence Ministers’ Dialogue held in Jun 2026. The two countries have continued to deepen cooperation in defence and security, including maritime security and regional cooperation.

During the visit, the CNS will hold bilateral discussions with the senior leadership of the RAN and engage with senior Australian defence leadership. The engagements will provide an opportunity to review ongoing naval cooperation and explore avenues for strengthening operational interaction, interoperability, information sharing, training and professional exchanges between the two navies.

The CNS will also visit key operational and training establishments and interact with personnel of the RAN. The engagements will include discussions on maritime capabilities, emerging technologies and professional military education, reflecting the expanding scope of cooperation between the two navies.

The visit to New Zealand builds upon the renewed momentum in India–New Zealand relations, following the visit of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to New Zealand in Jul 2026. During the visit, India and New Zealand elevated their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership and agreed to deepen cooperation across several areas, including defence and maritime security.

In New Zealand, the CNS will hold discussions with the senior leadership of the RNZN and engage with senior New Zealand defence leadership. The engagements will focus on further strengthening operational interaction, information sharing, training and professional exchanges between the two navies.

The CNS will also visit key operational and training establishments and interact with personnel of the Royal New Zealand Navy and officers undergoing professional military education. The visit assumes significance in the backdrop of the recently concluded Maritime Cooperation Arrangement, which provides an expanded framework for practical maritime cooperation between India and New Zealand.

The visit underscores India’s growing defence and maritime engagement with Australia and New Zealand and the commitment of the Indian Navy to further deepen cooperation with the Royal Australian Navy and Royal New Zealand Navy, through practical and sustained maritime engagement, contributing towards peace, security and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Union Minister of State for MSME Sushri Shobha Karandlaje to inaugurate Technology Centre at Devanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka
₹156 crore Technology Centre developed across 10 acres with state-of-the-art training, production and residential facilities
Centre to focus on Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM), strengthening industry-ready skills and capabilities
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

Hon’ble Minister of State for the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, will inaugurate the Technology Centre at Devanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka, on 10 September 2026. The inauguration ceremony will be graced by Shri Krishna Byre Gowda, Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development and Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Government of Karnataka, and Shri Vijayanand Kashappanavar, Minister of Small Scale Industries & Public Enterprises, Government of Karnataka, along with senior officers of the Ministry of MSME and the Government of Karnataka, representatives from industry and other local stakeholders. The inauguration ceremony will also feature an exhibition showcasing the contribution of Indian MSMEs to the Aerospace & ESDM Sectors.

 

The network of Technology Centres-         

To foster an enabling environment for MSMEs and enhance their technological capabilities and competitiveness, the Ministry of MSME operates a nation-wide network of Technology Centres (TCs).Over the years, these Centres have contributed significantly in technology development, industry-grade training, design, prototyping, testing & production support to MSMEs.
They are also contributing to the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat by building indigenous capabilities and advancing the initiative. Beyond supporting MSMEs, they contribute to national goals of technological self-reliance and sustainable industrial growth and globally competitive manufacturing ecosystem.     

Salient Features of Technology Centre (TC), Bengaluru

  • The TC Bengaluru has been developed by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India with an investment of ₹156 crore on a 10-acre land parcel provided by the Government of Karnataka. The TC features modern infrastructure, including a Training Block, Production Block, Administrative Block, residential facilities for boys and girls, staff accommodation, an executive hostel, and other supporting facilities.

  • Focus Sector of the centre is Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM). The Centre being equipped with state‑of‑the‑art machines and labs, will provide MSMEs access to advanced technologies such as Surface-Mount Technology (SMT) Line, additive manufacturing, CNC 5‑Axis and 3‑Axis machines, Electric Discharge Machine (EDM), etc. It will also offer comprehensive support through testing laboratories, design assistance, and business & technical advisory services to enhance MSMEs/Industry technological capabilities, productivity, and competitiveness.

  • The Centre catchment area has a strong ecosystem of leading industries and institutions such as Mitsubishi Electric India, Texas Instruments, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), National Aerospace Laboratories, (NAL), Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Airbus, Boeing, Philips, Wipro, GE, Centum Electronics etc., and numerous MSMEs engaged in aerospace, defence, semiconductor design, industrial automation, and advanced electronics manufacturing.
  • The Centre will also contribute towards skilling youth by providing industry grade training in the area of embedded system design, PCB Design and Assembly, automation & robotics, maintenance and repair, etc. TC is equipped to train 10,000 trainees every year.
  • The Technology Centre, Bengaluru is envisaged as a key institution for strengthening the MSME ecosystem in electronics and aerospace sectors through advanced design, prototyping, production, training, and consultancy services. The Centre is also expected to make a substantial contribution towards creating employment opportunities and promoting sustainable livelihoods in Karnataka.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
AIR DEFENCE EXERCISE WITH JASDF: EX VEER GUARDIAN-2026
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

            Indian Air Force (IAF) and the Japan Air Self Defence Force (JASDF) will conduct bilateral Air Exercise, Veer Guardian-2026, at Air Force Station Jodhpur, from                  09 Sep 26 to 22 Sep 2026.

            The Indian Air Force will participate with a diverse mix of frontline combat aircraft including indigenous Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas, Su-30 MKl and Rafale. JASDF will participate with its F-2A fighter aircraft.

            During the fourteen-day exercise, participating air warriors will undertake advanced operational missions and engage in extensive professional interactions. The program integrates mission planning conferences, subject matter expert exchanges, and interaction between personnel on engineering and aspects of aerospace safety, fostering deep operational synergy between the two Air Forces.

            Exercise Veer Guardian-26 reflects a deepening strategic partnership between India and Japan by enhancing tactical proficiency and aerospace operational synergy. The exercise reaffirms the longstanding bonds of friendship and strategic cooperation between the two nations.

***

JS/VK/GK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Bi-layered single-piece dental implant reduces the need for surgical interventions
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

Researchers have developed a bi-layered structure integrating titanium alloy and zirconia components for dental applications that enhances durability, interfacial stability, and biocompatibility while reducing surgical complexity.

Traditional dental implants consist of three components: a fixture embedded in the jawbone, an abutment connecting the fixture and crown, and the crown itself. These multi-component assemblies are susceptible to micromovements at the abutment interface, which can compromise osseointegration and lead to implant loosening.

Furthermore, such systems typically require two to three surgical procedures, increasing patient discomfort and clinical complexity. Although titanium alloys and zirconia are widely used due to their biocompatibility and mechanical strength, each material has inherent limitations. Ti6Al4V can be susceptible to corrosion and gum recession in the moist environment of the mouth, while zirconia, although aesthetically appealing and corrosion-resistant, may degrade over time due to hydrolysis, affecting its long-term stability.

To overcome these challenges, scientists at the International Advanced Research Centre for Powder Metallurgy and New Materials (ARCI), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) have designed a functionally integrated bi-layered structure that integrates titanium alloy (Ti6Al4V) and yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) into a unified structure to address persistent limitations of conventional implants.

Fig 1: (a) Schematic diagram of a tapered graphite die; (b) Schematic of the bi-layered Ti6Al4V-YSZ dental implant; (c) Bi-layer sample of 8YSZ (top) and Ti6Al4V (bottom); (d) cross section of the Bi-layered sample.

In the structure, the Ti6Al4V serves as the load-bearing fixture for strong jawbone integration, and YSZ forms the crown region to provide superior wear resistance and aesthetics.

The implant was fabricated using Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS), an advanced powder metallurgy technique. A custom-designed tapered graphite die enabled precise temperature control during sintering, allowing simultaneous densification of Ti6Al4V and YSZ, despite their widely differing sintering temperatures.

This approach achieved a density of 99.5% in the material, producing a strong, defect-free bi-layered structure in a single processing step. After sintering, machining trials were conducted using a 5-axis CNC machine to produce the threaded implant shape. Some challenges related to tool movement along curved surfaces were observed, and process optimization is currently underway.

The overall fabrication approach remains highly reproducible and suitable for scaling up to industrial production.

Tests confirmed a distinct, well-bonded interface without cracks, delamination, pores, or secondary phases. Analysis revealed fine YSZ grains (~0.3 µm), while Ti6Al4V grains near the interface were refined to 0.3–1 µm compared to the bulk. No noticeable elemental diffusion was observed across the interface, indicating a stable ceramic–metal transition zone. The fabrication route demonstrates high reproducibility, making the process scalable for industrial production.

 

Figure 2: (a) Region of Interest (ROI) of Bi-layered sample; (b) TKD-IPF; (c) TKD-phase map overlaid with Image Quality map for representation.

Mechanical evaluation of the dense, bi-layered structure showed hardness values up to 1350 HV, compressive strength of approximately 1550 MPa, and flexural strength of approximately 310 MPa, comparable to or exceeding those of commercial implant materials. In vitro biological studies confirmed non-cytotoxic behavior and excellent biocompatibility. MTT assays (colorimetric test used to measure cellular metabolic activity) using L929 mouse fibroblast cells showed metabolic activity exceeding 90% across all tested concentrations, surpassing the minimum threshold for biomaterials. Hemolysis tests indicated negligible red blood cell damage, validating suitability for dental applications.

By integrating mechanical robustness, corrosion resistance, aesthetic performance, and biological safety into a single-piece architecture, ARCI’s bi-layered implant reduces the need for surgical interventions while improving long-term stability and patient outcomes. The innovation aligns with India’s growing demand for affordable, high-performance dental implants and strengthens indigenous biomedical device development.

This work has been published in the journal Materials Letters on ScienceDirect.

Publication link: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matlet.2023.134403

For further clarifications, please contact: dibyenduc@arci.res.in

****

NKR/FT/AA

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM's speech during the 'Namo for Viksit Bharat' programme in Vadodara, Gujarat
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 4:23PM by PIB Delhi

भारत माता की जय।

भारत माता की जय।

गुजरात के राज्यपाल आचार्य देवव्रत जी, यहां के लोकप्रिय मुख्यमंत्री श्री भूपेंद्र भाई पटेल, इस कार्यक्रम में ऑनलाइन हमारे साथ अनेक राज्यों के महानुभाव जुड़े हैं। महाराष्ट्र के गवर्नर जिष्णु देव वर्मा जी, मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फ़डणवीस जी, डिप्टी सीएम एकनाथ शिंदे जी, डिप्टी सीएम श्रीमती सुनेत्र पवार जी, अन्य मंत्रीगण, सांसदगण, विधायकगण और वहां पर भी इकट्ठे हुए लाखों नागरिक भाई-बहन। यहां मंच पर उपस्थित केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल के मेरे साथी अश्विनी वैष्णव, उपमुख्यमंत्री, युवा नेता हर्ष संघवी, गुजरात सरकार के मंत्रीगण, उपस्थित अन्य जनप्रतिनिधिगण, गुजरात के मेरे प्यारे भाइयों और बहनों।

और खास इसलिए के मेरे ब़डौदा के महाराजा सयाजीराव यूनिवर्सिटी का ये मैदान अलग-अलग फील्ड में काम करने वाले सभी साथियों का साथ और विकास का ये उत्सव, यहां सबकुछ एक साथ हो रहा है।

साथियों,

आज मैं विकसित भारत की यात्रा को और गति देने के लिए आपके बीच आया हूं। थोड़ी देर पहले यहां देश के विकास से जुड़े हज़ारों करोड़ रुपए के प्रोजेक्ट्स का शिलान्यास और लोकार्पण हुआ है। मैं देश की जनता को बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं। इस विकास पर्व पर आप सभी ने जिस सेवा भाव से और सेवा भाव के साथ पूरे वडोदरा शहर में स्वच्छता से स्वागत अभियान चलाया है, इसके लिए मैं वड़ोदरा के हर एक नागरिक को ह्दय से बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं, उनकी सराहना करता हूं। और ये जो आपने रंग दिखाया ना, मैं कल एक वीडियो देख रहा था, सीना चौड़ा हो गया, वाह! क्या ये मेरा वडोदरा है? और अब तो गणेशोत्सव की तैयारी, बाद में नवरात्रि। और गणेशोत्सव और नवरात्रि पूरा गुजरात का ध्यान वडोदरा पर होता है। और आज आपने, मैं देख रहा था पिछले एक सप्ताह से हर परिवार में वातावरण बन गया है स्वच्छता का। मुझे लगता है कि इस बार जब गणेश जी पधारेंगे ना, सारे आशीर्वाद वड़ोदरा पर बरसने वाले हैं।

साथियों,

इस वर्ष लाल किले से मैंने विकसित भारत के लिए संकल्प की सप्तधारा का आह्वान किया है। इस सप्तधारा में एक धारा गतिशक्ति की भी है। विकसित भारत के लिए हमें ऐसी कनेक्टिविटी चाहिए, जो सुगम भी हो और जमाने के हिसाब से जरा तेज भी हो। वड़ोदरा तो गतिशक्ति यूनिवर्सिटी का शहर है। आज यहां से डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर की आखिरी कड़ियां भी जुड़ गई हैं। आज 2800 किलोमीटर से अधिक का डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर प्रोजेक्ट पूरा हो गया। ये 21वीं सदी के भारत के लिए बहुत ऐतिहासिक कार्य संपन्न हुआ है।

साथियों,

ये डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर, इस बात का साक्षी है कि बीते 12 साल में देश की काम करने की संस्कृति कैसे बदली है। इस डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर पर 2004 में विचार शुरू हुआ था। यानी, यहां मैं सारे नौजवान देख रहा हूं, जब इसका विचार शुरू हुआ, आप में से बहुत लोग होंगे जिनका जन्म भी नहीं हुआ होगा, उस समय शुरू हुआ था। 2006 में एक विशेष कंपनी बनाई गई इस काम को करने के लिए और फिर 2014 तक फाइलें ही यहां से वहां होती रहीं। फाइलें टेबल पर यात्रा कर रही थी और दुर्भाग्य देखिए, इन फाइलों को भी कोई डेडिकेटेड कॉरिडोर नसीब नहीं हुआ, फाइल को भी नहीं नसीब हुआ। फाइलें अटकती थीं, लटकती थीं, भटकती थीं। और 2014 में वड़ोदरा के और गुजरात के और देश के लोगों ने मुझे गुजरात से निकाल करके दिल्ली भेज दिया। पहले वाली सरकार 2000 तक रही। आपने मुझे भेजा और उनकी विदाई हुई, और सच्चाई ये थी कि सात-आठ वर्ष में, जरा मेरे नौजवान सुन लीजिए, ये याद रखिए, सात-आठ वर्ष में एक किलोमीटर फ्रेट कॉरिडोर पर भी काम पूरा नहीं हो पाया था। अगर उनके हिसाब से देश चलाते, तो पता नहीं आपके बाद तीन-चार पीढ़ियां आती, तो भी नहीं होता। भारत के लॉजिस्टिक्स इकोसिस्टम को ट्रांसफॉर्म करने वाले प्रोजेक्ट की ये हालत करके रखी थी।

साथियों,

2014 के बाद आपने जो मुझे शिक्षा-दीक्षा दी थी, इस धरती ने मुझे जो सिखाया था, आपके पास से जो लेसन लेके मैं दिल्ली पहुंचा था, हमने वहां पहुंचते ही इसको गति देने का काम प्रारंभ कर दिया। 2800 किलोमीटर के कॉरिडोर का काम आज पूरा करके दिखाया। और आज ईस्टर्न और वेस्टर्न डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर, देश के व्यापार-कारोबार का मुख्य आधार बन रहा है।

साथियों,

डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर, तेजी से विकसित होते भारत की जीवन रेखा है। इसने भारत के ट्रांसपोर्टेशन सेक्टर का कायाकल्प कर दिया है। पहले पैसेंजर ट्रेन जिस ट्रैक पर चलती थी, उसी ट्रैक पर मालगाड़ी भी चलती थी। यानि ट्रैवल और ट्रांसपोर्ट, दोनों धीमा था। लेकिन, डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर ने इस स्थिति को बदल दिया है। आज पूर्वी और पश्चिमी फ्रेट कॉरिडोर्स पर हर रोज़ 430 से ज्यादा मालगाड़ियां चलती हैं, प्रतिदिन 430 मालगाड़ी। और पहले जो मालगाड़ी, साढ़े 6 घंटे में 100 किलोमीटर का सफऱ तय करती थी और अब वही मालगाड़ी आधे से भी कम समय में 100 किलोमीटर का सफर तय कर लेगी। जिस जगह पर ट्रक से सामान भेजने में सामान्य तौर पर 30 घंटे लगते हैं, डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर पर यही दूरी 10-12 घंटे में पूरी हो जाती है। यानि, इस कॉरिडोर पर मालगाड़ी के चलने से ट्रक और ट्रेन में लगने वाला फ्यूल बचता है, किराया-भाड़ा का खर्च कम हुआ है, समय बचा है, पर्यावरण को फायदा हुआ है। यानि, इन्वेस्टमेंट एक ट्रैक पर किया और फायदे अनेक सारे हुए हैं।

साथियों,

इस फ्रेट कॉरिडोर से पूर्वी और पश्चिमी भारत के किसानों की उपज अब तेज़ी से बड़े बाज़ार तक पहुंच पा रही है। कई तरह के फूल, कई तरह की सब्जियां, कई तरह के फल, यानि जो चीजें मौसम के हिसाब से जल्दी खराब होती हैं, उनके लिए भी सही समय पर मंडियों और लोगों के बीच पहुंचने का रास्ता बना है। इससे किसान का बहुत बड़ा फायदा हुआ है।

साथियों,

ये फ्रेट कॉरिडोर एक और वजह से कमाल का है। हाल ही में JNPT मुंबई, JNPT पोर्ट से वड़ोदरा तक Double स्टैक Container मालगाड़ी का संचालन किया गया है। यानि डिब्बे के ऊपर एक और डिब्बा लगाकर मालगाड़ी को चलाया गया। इस मालगाड़ी के चलने से एक बार में ही 250 से अधिक ट्रकों के बराबर का सामान मुंबई से वड़ोदरा चला आया, 250 ट्रक। अब ये जो नाराज फूफा जी है, वो चिल्लाएंगे कि ट्रक वालों का क्या होगा? ट्रक कहां जाएंगे?  जिन्होंने ट्रक खरीदा है, उनका क्या होगा? अब फूफा जी को काम मिल गया। यानि अब बड़ी मात्रा में सामान तेजी से देश के एक कोने से दूसरे कोने तक पहुंच पाएगा।

साथियों,

फ्रेट कॉरिडोर के साथ-साथ अब भारत में रेल वहां भी पहुंच रही है, जहां इतने दशकों तक नहीं पहुंची थी। गुजरात हो, मध्य प्रदेश हो, महाराष्ट्र हो, यहां जो आदिवासी क्षेत्र हैं, वो भी इस प्रोजेक्ट के द्वारा रेल से जुड़ रहे हैं। पहले की सरकार में बजट में एक-दो ट्रेनों की घोषणा होती थी और उसके भी साल भर ढोल पीटे जाते थे। जबकि आज देश में साल भर एक के बाद एक नई ट्रेनें चलाई जा रही हैं। आज भी इस कार्यक्रम में कई नई ट्रेन शुरु हुई हैं। नई ट्रेन से वड़ोदरा, छोटा उदयपुर और अलीराजपुर के लोगों को बहुत सुविधा होगी।

साथियों,

रोड, रेल, मेट्रो, एयरपोर्ट, गैस पाइपलाइन, गरीबों का घर, जब देश में करोड़ों लोगों के लिए ये चीजें बनती हैं, तो इससे लोगों का जीवन आसान होता है और साथ ही छोटे से बड़े कामगार को रोजगार के लाखों-लाख अवसर मिलते हैं। आप रेलवे का ही देखिए, इस वर्ष का रेल बजट पौने तीन लाख करोड़ रुपए से अधिक रहा है। जो 12 वर्ष पहले की तुलना में कई गुणा अधिक है। यानि रेलवे के आधुनिकीकरण पर हो रहा खर्च, हज़ारों हज़ार नए रोजगार बना रहा है। और ये रोजगार कंस्ट्रक्शन के दौरान तो बनता ही है। एक बार रोड, रेल, पाइपलाइन, पोर्ट, एयरपोर्ट बन गया, तो फिर उसके आसपास नए उद्योग लगना शुरू हो जाते हैं, नए बिजनेस आते हैं, ये फिर नए रोजगार बनाते हैं। वहां कुछ लोग, वो बेटी चित्र लेकर कब से खड़ी है, वो सज्जन भी कुछ कला लेकर के आए हैं। जरा हमारे साथी उसको कलेक्ट कर लें। ये आगे पहुंचा दीजिए, हां। एक और भी है कोई, हां, ले लीजिए। आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

साथियों,

मैंने देश के सामने विकसित भारत की जिन सप्तधाराओं का विजन रखा है, उनमें एक धारा मैन्युफैक्चरिंग की भी है। और वड़ोदरा शहर, इसकी ताकत अच्छे से जानता भी है, समझता भी है। एजुकेशन, स्किल और इंडस्ट्री का कोलैब कैसे होता है, ये वड़ोदरा करीब डेढ़ सौ साल से इसका प्रतिबिंब है। दशकों पहले, यहां टेक्स्टाइल और टाइल्स के निर्माण से एक यात्रा शुरु हुई थी, जो बाद में ऑयल और पेट्रोकेमिकल्स के साथ आगे बढ़ी। पिछले दो-ढाई दशक में वड़ोदरा MSMEs का एक बड़ा हब बन गया है। और मुझे याद है, जब मैं नया-नया मुख्यमंत्री बना था, तो वड़ोदरा का मेरे पर स्पेशल अधिकार रहा है हमेशा, तो हर हफ्ते कोई ना कोई डेलीगेशन आता था। बस हमारे वड़ोदरा में कुछ मैन्युफैक्चरिंग का हो, मैन्युफैक्चरिंग का हो, क्योंकि यहां पर आते थे, तो या तो ज्योति या एलएमबी या तो जीएसएफसी, यही सब दिखता था और कुछ सुनता नहीं देता। आज कहां से कहां बदल गया है। अब तो ये शहर देश के पहले मेड इन इंडिया मिलिट्री ट्रांसपोर्ट एयरक्राफ्ट के लिए भी जाना जा रहा है। C-295 एयरक्राफ्ट की पहली फ्लाइट यहां आसमान देख चुकी है। मैं वड़ोदरा के लोगों को ये गौरव पाने के लिए बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं।

साथियों,

जब देश की मैन्युफैक्चरिंग की बात हो रही है, तो मैं एक और आंकड़ा बताना चाहता हूं। बीते एक दशक में भारत रेल कोच-मेट्रो कोच बनाने का, रेल इंजन बनाने का भी एक बड़ा निर्माता बना है। 2014 के बाद से अब तक, भारत ने करीब 50 हज़ार, ये आंकड़ा सुनिए, 2014 के बाद भारत ने अब तक 50 हज़ार आधुनिक रेलवे कोच बनाए हैं। पुरानी सरकार 10 साल में 50 हजार टॉयलेट नहीं बना सकती थी। 50 हजार आधुनिक कोच तो किए ही हैं, करीब ढाई लाख वेगन, मालगाड़ी के लिए जो वेगन होते हैं, भारतीय रेल में जोड़े गए हैं, ढाई लाख।

साथियों,

अब भारत चिप से लेकर शिप तक, निर्माण की एक नई गाथा लिख रहा है। यानि पुर्जे भी हमारे और प्रोडक्ट भी हमारा, आत्मनिर्भरता की एक पूरी चेन भारत में ही बनेगी। और ये हम सोलर पावर के मामले में देख रहे हैं। जैसे कडाणा डैम पर जो फ्लोटिंग सोलर प्लांट का प्रोजेक्ट है, कुछ साल पहले तक देश में सोलर प्रोजेक्ट्स लगाने बहुत महंगे पड़ते थे। क्योंकि पीवी मॉड्यूल से लेकर, हर प्रकार का हार्डवेयर इंपोर्ट करना पड़ता था। लेकिन बीते वर्षों में हमने भारत में ही पीवी मॉड्यूल बनाने शुरु किए। और आज हम इसमें 200 गीगावॉट से ज्यादा की कैपेसिटी विकसित कर चुके हैं। और ऐसी ही आत्मनिर्भरता के कारण आज पीएम सूर्यघर मुफ्त बिजली योजना का विस्तार हो रहा है। अब तक देश में 55 लाख परिवार अपने छत पर, टेरेस पर सोलर प्लांट लगा चुके हैं। और इसमें 11 लाख परिवार हमारे गुजरात के हैं। यहां इतने सारे परिवार, बिजली उत्पादक बन चुके हैं और इसके कारण, प्रोडक्शन से लेकर इंस्टॉलेशन और सर्विस तक, कितने ही युवाओं को रोजगार मिला है, कितने नए वेंडर्स आए हैं।

साथियों,

‘झूठ की गूंज’ से भरमाने वाले तो हर चौराहे पर मिल जाएंगे, लेकिन भारत का नौजवान सच की हुंकार से चलता है, सच की हुंकार के साथ चलता है, सच की हुंकार के लिए चलता है। हमारे युवा साथी ये देख रहे हैं कि आज देश में सोलर हो, विंड हो, हाइड्रो हो, न्यूक्लियर हो, सारे सेक्टर्स पर सरकार कितना फोकस से काम कर रही है।

साथियों,

आने वाले दौर में हर आधुनिक सेक्टर बिजली से ही चलेगा, इलेक्ट्रिक इकोसिस्टम पर निर्भर होगा। जैसे चिप इंडस्ट्री है, डेटा सेंटर और AI से जुड़ी इंडस्ट्री है, इनका खाद पानी बिजली ही है। इसलिए अगर हमें AI में दुनिया के सामने सुपर पावर बनना है, तो देश को उसकी तैयारी, उसका इकोसिस्टम भी बनाना होगा। यही काम भारत ग्राउंड पर कर रहा है। तभी किसी देश से यूरेनियम के लिए समझौते हो रहे हैं, किसी से क्रिटिकल मिनरल्स और रेयर अर्थ मिनरल्स को लेकर समझौते किए जा रहे हैं। ये सारी मेहनत देश के युवाओं का फ्यूचर सुरक्षित करने के लिए दिन-रात मेहनत करके की जा रही है, आपके भविष्य के लिए किया जा रहा है।

साथियों,

दुनिया तेज़ी से बदल रही है, तो दुनिया की ज़रूरतें भी बदल रही हैं और इसी प्रकार हमारी पढ़ाई-लिखाई के तौर-तरीके भी बदल रहे हैं। पहले फोकस सिर्फ डिग्री पर होता था, लेकिन अब डिग्री के साथ-साथ स्किल पर भी फोकस है, स्किल का महत्मय बढ़ रहा है। नौजवानों के पास स्किल हो और वो स्किल समय-समय पर अपग्रेड हो, एक बड़ी जरूरत बन गई है। और इसीलिए, आज हम अपनी शिक्षा नीति को, शिक्षण और ट्रेनिंग के संस्थानों को नए रूप में ढाल रहे हैं। और इसी भाव के साथ ही मैंने लाल किले से भी युवाशक्ति के लिए दो बड़ी घोषणाएं की हैं। पहली घोषणा, देश की पारंपरिक ज़रूरत से जुड़ी है। आप सब जानते हैं कि हमारे यहां लाखों नौजवान ऐसे हैं, जो प्रतियोगी परीक्षाओं की तैयारी करते हैं। हर साल, हमारे मिडिल क्लास परिवारों की कमाई का एक बड़ा हिस्सा इन बच्चों की कोचिंग पर खर्च हो जाता है। हमारी कोशिश है कि गरीब और मिडिल क्लास के ऐसे बच्चों की, परिवारों के पैसे की बचत हो। और इसीलिए अब सरकार स्टूडेंट्स को ऑनलाइन फ्री-कोचिंग व्यवस्था देने की दिशा में आगे बढ़ रही है। और हिंदुस्तान के बेस्ट टीचर के द्वारा उनके कोचिंग हो। हमारे जो नौजवान, अपनी तैयारी कर रहे हैं, उनकी कोचिंग का ध्यान सरकार खुद रखेगी।

साथियों,

भारत के नौजवानों को AI में पारंगत होना उतना ही जरूरी है। हम चाहते हैं कि हमारे नौजवानों की पीढ़ी AI के लिए तैयार हो। ऐसा नहीं है, AI सीखने वालों की जरूरत सिर्फ आईटी सेक्टर में है, अगर कोई इस स्किल को जानता है, तो वो खेती के लिए नया AI solution बना सकता है। आरोग्य के क्षेत्र में technology विकसित कर सकता है। Manufacturing की productivity बढ़ा सकता है। Robotics में अपना startup शुरू कर सकता है। इसलिए जरूरी है कि हमारे पास देश और दुनिया की इंडस्ट्री के लिए AI को समझने वाले और AI का इस्तेमाल करने वाले युवा हों। सरकार इसके लिए एक बड़ा अभियान शुरू करने जा रही है।

साथियों,

भारत का ये कालखंड अभूतपूर्व है। ये भारत की युवाशक्ति का उत्कर्ष काल है, ये समय फिर भारत के जीवन में लौटकर नहीं आएगा। और इसलिए, हमें 2047 में विकसित भारत के लक्ष्य को सर्वोपरि रखना है। हमें भारत को विकसित बनाकर ही रहना है। इसी आह्वान के साथ, एक बार फिर आप सभी को विकास कार्यों की बहुत शुभकामनाएं।

अब मेरा एक काम करना पड़ेगा वडोदरा वालों को, करेंगे? पक्के तौर पर? आप सबने वड़ोदरा को इतना स्वच्छ बना दिया, कितनी मेहनत करनी पड़ी। मैं देख रहा था, हमारे नौजवान दिन-रात सफाई में लगे हुए थे। लेकिन एक बार हम तय करें कि अब हम वडोदरा को गंदा होने ही नहीं देंगे। मैं खुद गंदगी नहीं करूँगा, ये संकल्प लें, तो वडोदरा गंदा होगा? वडोदरा गंदा होगा? तो दिवाली ऐसी चकाचक जाएगी या नहीं, नवरात्रि शानदार जाएगी या नहीं, गणेशोत्सव में चार चाँद लगेंगे या नहीं, तो इतना काम तो हो जाएगा।

शाबाश।

धन्यवाद।

भारत माता की जय!

भारत माता की जय!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

वंदे मातरम्!

 

डिस्क्लेमर: प्रधानमंत्री के भाषण का कुछ अंश गुजराती भाषा में भी है, जिसका यहाँ भावानुवाद किया गया है।

*****

MJPS/SS/SS/RK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
IAF DRONATHON 2026
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi

IAF is organising Dronathon-2026 with an aim to offer domestic manufacturers to exhibit their capabilities and advancements in Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) and Counter Unmanned Aerial Systems (CUAS). The event is designed to help stakeholders to witness emerging drone and counter drone technologies along with their operational demonstration and foster mutual learning.

The event is scheduled to take place at Pokhran range, Jaisalmer from 14 to      16 Sep 26. The event comprises of static display and live demonstrations. It will help to identify contemporary solutions and evaluate their combat effectiveness. Key areas of focus include surveillance and reconnaissance, autonomous operations, swarm technologies, and electronic warfare.

Aligning with the national vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat. Dronathon-2026 aims to bolster the indigenous defence ecosystem by integrating industry experts, start-ups, and innovators. Through such initiatives, the IAF remains committed to building a technologically advanced, indigenous and future ready force capable of meeting security challenges in the rapidly changing operational environment.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
DFPD and FCI Sign MoU for FY 2026–27 to Strengthen Efficiency, Technology and Accountability in Foodgrain Management
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 3:11PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Food & Public Distribution (DFPD) and the Food Corporation of India (FCI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the Financial Year 2026–27 in New Delhi. The MoU establishes a comprehensive performance framework for FCI, with defined targets aimed at improving operational efficiency, strengthening accountability and accelerating modernisation in foodgrain management.

The MoU focuses on key areas including reduction of storage losses, optimal utilisation of storage capacity, improvement in logistics and supply chain management, and strengthening of quality control mechanisms. It also places emphasis on greater digitisation of business processes and adoption of modern Information Technology solutions to enhance efficiency, transparency and monitoring of FCI’s operations.

As part of the modernisation agenda, the MoU provides for capacity building and skill development initiatives for FCI employees, enabling the organisation to effectively adopt emerging technologies and contemporary systems of foodgrain management.

Established in 1965 under the Food Corporations Act, 1964, FCI plays a pivotal role in maintaining the country’s food security by undertaking procurement, storage, movement and distribution of foodgrains on behalf of the Government of India. Given the scale of public resources involved in its operations, efficient utilisation of food subsidy and continuous improvement in operational processes remain key priorities.

The MoU introduces a measurable and outcome-oriented approach to FCI’s functioning by linking its performance with clearly defined annual parameters. The framework is intended to promote greater efficiency in the utilisation of resources, strengthen transparency in operations and encourage adoption of technology-driven solutions across the organisation.

A proportion of the MoU targets has been linked to the performance of FCI’s depots through the Depot Darpan Portal, a web-based platform for assessing depot infrastructure and operational efficiency. Outcome- and target-based benchmarks have been incorporated to strengthen physical infrastructure, improve operational performance and promote continuous improvement across FCI depots.

The signing of the MoU reflects the Government’s continued commitment towards modernising the foodgrain management system and enhancing the efficiency and resilience of the country’s food security architecture. Through this performance-based framework, DFPD and FCI reaffirm their commitment to ensuring that food subsidy resources are utilised in a cost-effective and transparent manner while delivering greater value to the nation.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi lays foundation stones, inaugurates and dedicates to the Nation development projects worth more than ₹35,000 Crore In Vadodara, Gujarat
We are strengthening India's infrastructure to move people and goods faster, create new opportunities and power economic growth: PM
The Dedicated Freight Corridor is the lifeline of a rapidly developing India: PM
From chips to ships, India is now building a new manufacturing future: PM
Posted On: 08 SEP 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi laid foundation stones, inaugurated and dedicated to the Nation development projects worth more than ₹35,000 Crore in Vadodara, Gujarat. Extending warm greetings to the esteemed dignitaries, the Prime Minister commenced his address. He welcomed the citizens joining the monumental occasion both physically and via online mediums. "I welcome my brothers and sisters of Gujarat,” remarked Shri Modi.

Highlighting the vibrant atmosphere at the Maharaja Sayajirao University ground, the Prime Minister celebrated the unique convergence of professionals from diverse fields gathering for a shared festival of progress. He expressed immense joy at witnessing such a unified celebration of development. "Everything is happening here simultaneously,” noted Shri Modi.

Dedicating infrastructure projects worth thousands of crores to accelerate national progress, the Prime Minister expressed deep appreciation for the exceptional cleanliness drive organized by the citizens of Vadodara to welcome him. He thanked the local population for their profound spirit of service during this festival of development. "Today I have come among you to give further momentum to the journey of a Viksit Bharat,” asserted Shri Modi.

Outlining the 'Saptadhara' (seven streams) resolution announced at the Red Fort, the Prime Minister emphasized the critical need for rapid connectivity through the Gati Shakti initiative, marking the historic completion of the 2800-kilometer Dedicated Freight Corridor. He praised Vadodara as the true city of Gati Shakti University where the final links of this massive project were connected. "This historic task for 21st-century India has been accomplished,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Showcasing the accelerated momentum post-2014, the Prime Minister celebrated the successful execution of the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors which are now fundamentally transforming the commercial landscape. He noted that these networks are rapidly becoming the bedrock of the nation's commerce. "We gave it momentum and demonstrated it by completing the work of the 2800-kilometer corridor,” asserted Shri Modi.

Elaborating on the transformative impact of this new national lifeline, the Prime Minister detailed how separating passenger and freight traffic allows over 430 cargo trains to run daily, slashing a 30-hour truck journey to just 10-12 hours. He explained that covering 100 kilometers now takes less than half the previous time, saving fuel, reducing freight charges, and protecting the environment. "The investment was made on one track, but it yielded numerous benefits,” noted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the profound agricultural benefits of the expanded logistics network, the Prime Minister explained how farmers across Eastern and Western India can now swiftly transport perishable goods to larger markets. He emphasized that sensitive items like seasonal flowers, vegetables, and fruits are finally reaching consumers and mandis right on time. "This has immensely benefited the farmers,” remarked Shri Modi.

Sharing a remarkable operational milestone on the new corridor, the Prime Minister praised the successful deployment of a double-stack container freight train from JNPT Port to Vadodara. He pointed out that this single train journey efficiently transported cargo equivalent to more than 250 trucks straight from Mumbai. "Large quantities of goods will now be able to reach from one corner of the country to another rapidly,” observed Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister underscored his administration's continuous rollout of new rail services that are finally penetrating isolated tribal regions across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra. He celebrated a newly launched train that will immensely benefit commuters traveling to Chhota Udepur and Alirajpur. "Rail is now reaching those parts of India where it had not reached for decades,” asserted Shri Modi.

Detailing the massive macroeconomic ripple effects of infrastructure development spanning roads, metros, airports, and gas pipelines, the Prime Minister cited the historic railway budget of over 2.75 lakh crore rupees as a primary engine for generating millions of employment opportunities. He explained that building houses for the poor and expanding ports naturally incubates new industries and businesses in the surrounding areas. "The expenditure happening on the modernization of the railways is creating thousands upon thousands of new jobs,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Transitioning to the manufacturing pillar of his 'Saptadhara' vision, the Prime Minister lauded Vadodara's 150-year legacy of industrial evolution from textiles to petrochemicals, and its massive growth as an MSME hub over the last two decades. He proudly acknowledged the city's crowning achievement as the birthplace of India's first domestically manufactured military transport aircraft. "The first flight of the C-295 aircraft has already seen the sky here,” remarked Shri Modi.

Illustrating the country's surging industrial capacity over the past decade, the Prime Minister presented robust statistics showcasing India's transformation into a major global manufacturer of modern railway coaches, wagons, and locomotive engines. He specified that since 2014, the nation has successfully produced 50,000 modern coaches and introduced nearly 2.5 lakh wagons to the railway network. "India has become a major manufacturer of rail coaches, metro coaches, and rail engines,” noted Shri Modi.

Championing the drive toward total self-reliance across critical supply chains, the Prime Minister highlighted the domestic production of solar PV modules which slashed previously exorbitant import costs and built a massive 200 GW capacity. He celebrated the success of the Kadana Dam floating solar project and the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which has empowered 55 lakh families nationwide, including 11 lakh in Gujarat, to become electricity producers and generate immense local employment. "India is now writing a new saga of manufacturing from chip to ship,” asserted Shri Modi.

Dismissing the echoes of lies propagated by detractors, the Prime Minister expressed deep faith in the youth who witnessed the government's intense focus across solar, wind, hydro, and nuclear sectors. He praised the younger generation for recognizing the massive strides being made in national development. "The youth of India walks with the roar of truth,” affirmed Shri Modi.'

Emphasizing the strategic necessity of a robust electric ecosystem to power emerging technologies like data centers and artificial intelligence, the Prime Minister confirmed that international agreements for uranium, critical minerals, and rare earth elements are being actively secured. He stated that creating this essential infrastructure is critical if the nation is to become a global superpower in AI. "All this hard work is being done solely to secure the future of the country's youth,” asserted Shri Modi.

Addressing the shifting paradigms of the modern global economy, the Prime Minister stressed that traditional degrees are no longer sufficient, prompting a comprehensive restructuring of the National Education Policy to prioritize continuous skill enhancement. He noted that teaching and training institutions are being entirely remolded to meet the evolving demands of the world. "It has become a massive necessity for the youth to possess skills and for those skills to be upgraded,” observed Shri Modi.'

Fulfilling a crucial commitment made from the Red Fort, the Prime Minister announced a landmark initiative to provide free coaching for competitive exams, aiming to alleviate the immense financial strain on poor and middle-class households. He assured that the administration will take direct responsibility for supporting the aspirations of students preparing for their careers. "The government itself will take care of the coaching of our youth,” affirmed Shri Modi.'

Recognizing artificial intelligence as a foundational capability transcending the IT sector, the Prime Minister unveiled plans for a massive national campaign to cultivate AI-proficient youth capable of driving innovations in agriculture, healthcare, and robotics. He emphasized that mastering these cutting-edge tools will boost manufacturing productivity and spark innovative startups. "We want our younger generation to be ready for AI,” asserted Shri Modi.

Concluding with a powerful call to action, the Prime Minister urged the nation to capitalize on this unprecedented demographic dividend, maintaining an unwavering focus on transforming the country by 2047. He ended his address by offering his best wishes for the ongoing development works. "We must relentlessly ensure India becomes developed,” affirmed Shri Modi.

We are strengthening India's infrastructure to move people and goods faster, create new opportunities and power economic growth. Addressing a programme in Vadodara during the launch of key projects. https://t.co/JfapjA64fm

Rice: About 421.82 lakh ha area coverage under rice has been reported as compared to 438.19 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 16.37 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Karnataka (4.28 lakh ha), Telangana (3.61 lakh ha), Uttar Pradesh (1.84 lakh ha), Andhra Pradesh (1.91 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (1.75 lakh ha), Tamil Nadu (1.32 lakh ha), Jharkhand (1.38 lakh ha), Maharashtra (1.15 lakh ha), etc. Higher area coverage has been reported in Assam (0.52 lakh ha), Odisha (0.29 lakh ha), etc.. Overall, the decline in rice area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Karnataka, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra.

 

Pulses: About 117.13 lakh ha area coverage under pulses has been reported as compared to 115.30 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing an increase of 1.84 lakh ha. The major increase in area coverage has been reported in Uttar Pradesh (3.97 lakh ha), Jharkhand (0.98 lakh ha), Telangana (0.90 lakh ha), Rajasthan (0.57 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.38 lakh ha) etc. On the other hand, the major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Maharashtra (2.60 lakh ha), Karnataka (2.07 lakh ha), Odisha (0.61 lakh ha) etc. Overall, the increase in pulses area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial gains in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, which more than offset the declines reported in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Odisha.

Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals: About 181.39 lakh ha area coverage under Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals has been reported as compared to 182.48 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 1.09 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Karnataka (5.64 lakh ha), Maharashtra (2.41 lakh ha), Andhra Pradesh (0.62 lakh ha), Tamil Nadu (0.24 lakh ha) etc. The higher area coverage has been reported in Rajasthan (2.90 lakh ha), Chhattisgarh (1.69 lakh ha), Odisha (0.85 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.80 lakh ha), Bihar (0.72 lakh ha), Uttar Pradesh (0.63 lakh ha), Jharkhand (0.41 lakh ha), Uttarakhand (0.38 lakh ha), etc. Overall, the decline in area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Karnataka and Maharashtra, along with declines in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, which have more than offset the gains recorded in Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.

 

Oilseeds: About 191.99 lakh ha area coverage under oilseeds has been reported as compared to 193.06 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 1.07 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Rajasthan (2.23 lakh ha), Gujarat (1.93 lakh ha), Karnataka (0.37 lakh ha), etc. The higher area coverage has been reported in Uttar Pradesh (2.91 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (1.14 lakh ha), etc. Overall, the decline in oilseed area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Rajasthan and Gujarat, which have more than offset the gains recorded in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

 

Sugarcane: About 58.47 lakh ha area coverage under sugarcane has been reported as compared to 58.87 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.40 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Bihar (0.30 lakh ha), Uttarakhand (0.20 lakh ha), etc. The higher area coverage has been reported in Uttar Pradesh (0.36 lakh ha), Haryana (0.21 lakh ha), etc. Overall, the decline in sugarcane area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Bihar and Uttarakhand followed, which have more than offset the gains recorded in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana.

 

Jute & Mesta: About 6.34 lakh ha area coverage under Jute & Mesta has been reported as compared to 6.24 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing an increase of 0.10 lakh ha. The major increase in area coverage has been reported in Bihar (0.11 lakh ha), West Bengal (0.06 lakh ha), etc. On the other hand, the decrease in area coverage has been reported in Assam (0.07 lakh ha), Pradesh (0.01 lakh ha) etc., Overall, the increase in Jute & Mesta area is mainly attributable to higher coverage in Bihar and West Bengal, which have more than offset the decline reported in Assam and Andhra Pradesh.

Cotton: About 109.17 lakh ha area coverage under cotton has been reported as compared to 109.87 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.69 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Rajasthan (1.05 lakh ha), Haryana (0.90 lakh ha), Punjab (0.43 lakh ha), etc. On the other hand, higher area coverage has been reported mainly in Telangana (1.14 lakh ha), Gujarat (0.66 lakh ha), etc.. Overall, the decline in cotton area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Rajasthan and Haryana, followed by declines in Punjab, which have more than offset the gains recorded in Telangana and Gujarat.
