item.title: India–EU FTA Opens Huge Opportunities for Farmers, MSMEs, Innovators, Startups and Businesses in India and Europe: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry India–EU FTA Opens Huge Opportunities for Farmers, MSMEs, Innovators, Startups and Businesses in India and Europe: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Belgian PM Bart De Wever says India–EU FTA will strengthen trade, investment and economic resilience; highlights Port of Antwerp-Bruges as key India–Europe link India and Belgium can deepen cooperation in gems and jewellery, semiconductors, green hydrogen, defence and advanced manufacturing, and agriculture and food processing: Shri Goyal India–EU FTA brings together a market of 2 billion people,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India–EU FTA Opens Huge Opportunities for Farmers, MSMEs, Innovators, Startups and Businesses in India and Europe: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal
Belgian PM Bart De Wever says India–EU FTA will strengthen trade, investment and economic resilience; highlights Port of Antwerp-Bruges as key India–Europe link
India and Belgium can deepen cooperation in gems and jewellery, semiconductors, green hydrogen, defence and advanced manufacturing, and agriculture and food processing: Shri Goyal
India–EU FTA brings together a market of 2 billion people, representing a quarter of global GDP and a third of world trade: Shri Goyal
India–EU trade has doubled in the last decade to nearly USD 140 billion; Port of Antwerp-Bruges can serve as a gateway for Indian exports into Europe
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 7:03PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today said that the India–European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement (FTA) opens huge opportunities for farmers, fishermen, MSMEs, small industries, innovators, startups, women entrepreneurs, manufacturers and service providers in India and Europe. Addressing the India–Belgium High-Level Dialogue on the India–EU FTA in Mumbai, in the presence of Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Belgium Mr. Bart De Wever and Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Shri Goyal said the agreement had been deftly negotiated while protecting sensitive sectors on both sides.

Shri Goyal said the India–EU FTA, which was in the making for 25 years before negotiations were concluded under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, brings together 2 billion people, representing a quarter of global GDP, a third of world trade and a market of USD 24 trillion. He said all 27 EU countries were on board, supportive and desirous of concluding the formalities and bringing the agreement into force at the earliest. He noted that such unanimous support was, as he understood, rare in the European context. Similarly, every section in India had supported the India–EU FTA wholeheartedly.

Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Belgium Mr. Bart De Wever said the India–EU FTA would strengthen trade and open doors for companies, young talent and investment, while making the two economies more resilient against disruptions. Highlighting the Port of Antwerp-Bruges as an important logistical link between India and Europe, he said the FTA would create opportunities in areas including diamonds, food processing, pharmaceuticals, maritime services, green hydrogen and infrastructure, and noted that tariffs on more than 95 per cent of Indian and European goods exports would be scrapped or reduced.

The Union Minister said India and Belgium have a significant opportunity to deepen economic cooperation as their economies complement each other across five major areas. He said India and Belgium could explore co-creation and design in gems and jewellery, including lab-grown diamonds as a new area of cooperation. He called for greater cooperation in technology and certification for mutual recognition, anchored around the main diamond centres of Antwerp, Mumbai and Surat.

Shri Goyal said Belgium’s world-class micro-electronics research could be paired with India’s scale, skills and talent to create a design-to-fabrication ecosystem in semiconductors. He said India’s Green Hydrogen Mission could power Europe through Antwerp-Bruges’ bunkering and green shipping infrastructure and called for deeper collaboration in this area.

Referring to the exchange of Memoranda of Understanding with John Cockerill, Shri Goyal said there was significant potential for cooperation in defence and advanced manufacturing, including counter-drone systems, electronic warfare, precision munitions and Western export corridors for India-designed BrahMos and Pinaka missiles. He said industrial alignment between India and Belgium had never run deeper. He also noted that John Cockerill makes ammunition for India’s Bofors guns. Given increased spending in Europe under the new conditions and India’s own security environment, he said there was tremendous potential to work together.

Shri Goyal also highlighted opportunities in agriculture and food processing, ranging from potato processing and cold chains to other areas of food processing. He said technology and sustainable agri-value chains could serve the entire world through Belgium and India.

The Union Minister said Belgium stands at the gateway of the opportunity created by the India–EU FTA. He noted that the Port of Antwerp-Bruges is Europe’s second-largest seaport and described it as the doorway through which the FTA’s promise would physically arrive in Europe or be dispatched to India. He said that by seamlessly combining Antwerp’s world-class inland barge, rail and road networks with Bruges’ seabridges, deepwater, roll-on/roll-off and automotive strengths, the port offers Indian exporters an unmatched route into the industrial and consumer heartlands of Europe.

Shri Goyal said India’s trade with the EU had already doubled over the last decade to nearly USD 140 billion. He said India and Belgium had a choice in the face of protectionism, broken supply chains, problems in food and fuel delivery, two wars, volatility, uncertainty and major challenges, to either be swept by the prevailing chaos or build islands of trust and predictability.

Quoting Belgian Nobel laureate Ilya Prigogine, Shri Goyal referred to the idea of “order emerging out of chaos” and said that under the leadership of the Prime Minister of Belgium and the Prime Minister of India, “we choose to build, we choose to connect, we choose to work together.”

Shri Goyal highlighted India’s expanding economic and technological capabilities and said that the Indian story had just begun. He noted that India is a USD 4 trillion economy today on a purchasing power parity basis and is already the world’s third-largest economy with a USD 20 trillion GDP on a PPP basis. He said the stated goal and collective commitment of 1.4 billion Indians was to take the USD 4 trillion economy to a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047, when India celebrates 100 years of independence.

He said the roadmap had been made and the collective effort underway in India covered social upliftment, infrastructure creation, manufacturing at scale and creating a destination for global companies to come and work in India, design, co-design, co-create and co-manufacture. He said India and its partners could collectively work not only for Europe and India, but for the world as their market.

Shri Goyal highlighted India’s massive programme to promote the semiconductor industry. He said the first edition of Semicon India had been fully subscribed, with investors from around the world, while the second edition, Semicon India 2.0, had recently been launched with an outlay of USD 14 billion. Collectively, he said, the mission would catalyse nearly USD 70 billion worth of investments in the semiconductor space in India.

He said India’s AI Mission was up and running and serving startups, while the country was also active in its Critical Minerals Mission. He said India’s nuclear energy programme, through the Shanti Act, was now open to the private sector after 60 years, with a plan to build 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity over the next 20 years as baseload capacity to replace fossil fuel.

Shri Goyal said India’s space technology sector, currently at USD 8.5 billion, was expected to grow to USD 44 billion over the next eight years, largely driven by new private initiatives, startups, innovators and designers developing unique solutions. He said India had become only the third country in the world where a private company had launched a rocket into space and the first country where a private initiative had been successful on its very first attempt.

He also highlighted India’s recently launched USD 12 billion research and development fund for innovation. He said that, while USD 12 billion might appear modest from the European context, India’s purchasing power parity strength meant that the government’s contribution, coupled with private-sector investment and the capabilities of India’s academia, could collectively deliver the equivalent of USD 150 billion of innovation compared to what could be achieved in Europe, at a fraction of the cost and comparable to the best in the world.

Shri Goyal invited Belgium and the European Union to partner with India, saying that Belgium’s technology, innovation and capital could find a nest in India with its scale, talent, youthful energy, young population and decisive leadership.

The Union Minister said Maharashtra offered a very inviting place for business, describing it as India’s financial and commercial capital, its industrial capital and the fastest-growing economy in the country.

Shri Goyal invited Prime Minister De Wever and Belgian companies to engage with India with an open mind and open heart, supported by all the facilities required by modern industry. He said that underpinning all these opportunities were people, including the Indian community, students and researchers.

The Union Minister called for strengthening workforce mobility, mutual recognition of qualifications, joint skills development and dual-degree education programmes, particularly in sectors where Belgium faces a shortage of talent and youth.

Shri Goyal said India and Belgium share a very warm and enduring relationship dating back to 1947, when India gained independence. He noted that Belgium was one of the first European countries to establish diplomatic relations with independent India and said India would always be grateful to the Belgian people for the gesture.

The Union Minister thanked Prime Minister De Wever for his leadership, support and relentless pursuit of strengthening Belgium–India and EU–India relations, which had helped culminate a journey of 25 years.

Shri Goyal said that during his recent visit to Belgium, referred to during the programme, the real energy he felt was in Belgian enterprises. He said Belgium and India, together, could create an “absolutely unbeatable competition” by combining Belgian technology, innovation and capital with India’s scale, talent, youthful energy, young population and decisive leadership.

Concluding his address, Shri Goyal drew an analogy with the formation of a diamond. He said a diamond is formed under tremendous pressure, deep under the ground, while lab-grown diamonds are formed through relentless processes involving carbon deposits. He said that in a world under pressure and turmoil, India and Belgium could form something equally enduring, beautiful and precious as a diamond.

“Let India and Belgium form something just as enduring, just as beautiful and precious as a diamond. A diamond not only for Belgium and India, a diamond not only for Europe, a diamond for the world,” Shri Goyal said.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Abhijith Narayanan/ Ishita Biswas

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Steel
SAIL posts strong sales and production growth in August 2026; financial position strengthens
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 6:40PM by PIB Delhi

Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) has reported a strong upward trend in sales performance for August 2026 as well as the April - August 2026 period. August 2026 also marked a milestone on the production front, with the company achieving its best ever August output of hot metal, crude steel and saleable steel. In August, 2026 the crude steel production grew by 8% to 1.68 MT over 1.55 MT in the corresponding period last year, hot metal rose by 9% to 1.78 MT over 1.63 MT, and saleable steel registered a 1% increase to 1.69 MT compared to 1.66 MT in CPLY.

In August 2026, SAIL achieved double digit year on year growth in overall sales volumes, with notable traction across Tier 1 and Tier 2 retail channels. Total sales stood at 1.871 million tonnes, registering a 13% y‑o‑y increase over the CPLY figure of 1.654 million tonnes. Cash collections also grew strongly by 23% y‑o‑y.

The Company recorded its highest ever August sales in several value added product categories like cold rolled, galvanized and alloy steels. The month additionally saw a meaningful reduction in inventory, indicating efficient supply chain coordination and faster market servicing. During August 2026, the rail supplies to Indian railways grew by 5% y-o-y to 1.23 Lakh Tonnes over 1.18 Lakh Tonnes in CPLY. In the Long Rails category, the company achieved highest ever supplies by supplying 1.12 Lakh Tonnes, with growth of 11% y-o-y. During this period, SAIL further strengthened its financial position, reducing borrowings by ₹870 crore from the 31.03.2026 level.

The momentum continued through the April - August 2026 period. SAIL’s cumulative sales reached 7.71 million tonnes scoring a growth of 5.6% over CPLY, despite global volatility. Finished and processed steel segments maintained healthy movement, supported by an improved product mix, stronger regional outreach and firm domestic demand. Cash collections for the five month period also grew, reflecting disciplined commercial practices and timely customer realisations.

Commenting on the performance, Dr. A.K. Panda, Chairman & Managing Director, SAIL, said: “SAIL’s performance in August and the April-August’26 period reflects the organization’s growing alignment between operational capability, commercial delivery and financial prudence. The record production levels, strong sales momentum and disciplined financial management together underscore the Company’s strengthening fundamentals. With expansion projects progress and demand outlook remaining positive, SAIL is well positioned to accelerate its growth trajectory while contributing meaningfully to India’s steel consumption story.”

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF TEACHERS’ DAY
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 5:38PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu has greeted teachers across the country on the eve of Teachers’ Day.

In a message, the President has said, “On the occasion of Teachers’ Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings to all our teachers across the country. Teachers’ Day is observed to mark the birth anniversary of the former President of India, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan who was a great author and philosopher. He was also an extraordinary teacher. On this occasion, I pay my humble tributes to him.

Teachers, through their guidance and mentorship, play a vital role in nurturing talent and strengthening character. It is their duty to guide students to become good human beings.  A dedicated and caring teacher can recognise the unique potential of students, serve as a source of inspiration and encourage them to strive for excellence. 

The teachers should continually update their knowledge, embrace technology and adopt innovative teaching methods. They should promote independent thinking and cultivate a spirit of enquiry among students.

I express my gratitude to all the dedicated teachers for their contribution. I wish that all teachers nurture enlightened generations who will take the nation to greater heights”.

 

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
ECL Launches Special Campaign 6.0 to Drive Cleanliness, Sustainability and Operational Efficiency.
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 5:27PM by PIB Delhi

Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) has launched Special Campaign 6.0 under ‘Waste to Wealth’ theme by Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances and ‘eWaste Management’ theme by Ministry of Coal, GoI, reaffirming its commitment towards enhancing workplace cleanliness, promoting sustainability and strengthening operational efficiency across the organisation.

The campaign will focus on Effective collection, Segregation and Disposal of e-waste through four key areas—E-Waste Management, Pendency Reduction, Space Optimisation and Digitalisation—with a comprehensive action plan to be implemented in two phases. The Preparatory Phase will be undertaken from September 15 to September 30, 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from October 2 to October 31, 2026.

 


The campaign was formally launched by CMD, ECL, Shri Satish Jha, who gave the green signal for its commencement. Addressing the gathering, Shri Jha emphasised the importance of collective participation in achieving the objectives of Special Campaign 6.0 and called upon employees to make active and meaningful contributions towards its successful implementation.

The launch programme was attended by Director (Finance) Shri Md. Anzar Alam; Director (HR) Shri Gunjan Kumar Sinha; Director (Technical/P&P) Shri Girish Gopinathan Nair and Director (Technical/Operations) Shri Chitranjan Kumar, Nodal Officer – Special Campaign 6.0, Shri Nazrul Islam, General Manager (HR) along with HODs from HQ and General Managers of various Areas.

 


Under Special Campaign 6.0, ECL will undertake focused measures with ‘Act Today, Impact Tomorrow’ for the systematic collection, segregation and responsible disposal of electronic waste, while strengthening efforts towards the timely disposal of pending public grievances, appeals, references and communications received from various stakeholders, including Members of Parliament and State Governments.

The campaign will also emphasise space optimisation through the identification and disposal of scrap, obsolete and unserviceable items occupying valuable office space. In addition, ECL will promote paperless and eco-friendly workplace practices, leveraging digitalisation to enhance efficiency and reduce environmental impact.

item.dc:creator: Department of Space
item.description: Department of Space Dr Jitendra Singh and French Minister Philippe Baptiste hold virtual meeting; discuss upcoming 'International Space Summit' and France’s participation in 'Bengaluru Space Expo' India-France Space Partnership to Gain Further Momentum with Focus on Human Spaceflight, Advanced Technologies and Industry Cooperation Chairman ISRO invited to deliver keynote on India’s future human spaceflight in Low Earth Orbit at Paris Summit French Minister Philippe Baptiste to visit ISRO facilities in Bengaluru later this month Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 4:33PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Department of Space
Dr Jitendra Singh and French Minister Philippe Baptiste hold virtual meeting; discuss upcoming 'International Space Summit' and France’s participation in 'Bengaluru Space Expo'
India-France Space Partnership to Gain Further Momentum with Focus on Human Spaceflight, Advanced Technologies and Industry Cooperation
Chairman ISRO invited to deliver keynote on India’s future human spaceflight in Low Earth Orbit at Paris Summit
French Minister Philippe Baptiste to visit ISRO facilities in Bengaluru later this month
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 4:33PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, held a bilateral meeting virtually with France’s Minister for Higher Education, Research and Space, Prof Philippe Baptiste, with the two sides agreeing to further deepen India-France cooperation in space, including in human spaceflight, advanced space technologies and greater engagement between their space agencies and industries.

The discussions took place ahead of the International Space Summit, scheduled for September 9-10, 2026 in Paris, and the Bengaluru Space Expo, scheduled for September 7-9, 2026. Both sides discussed India’s participation in the Paris Summit and France’s participation in the Bengaluru Space Expo, along with the forthcoming visit of Prof. Baptiste to India later this month.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India looks forward to participating in the International Space Summit and to further strengthening its longstanding space partnership with France. He said the Summit’s focus on space science, technology and applications, space economy and secure space provide an important platform for international dialogue and cooperation on the future of the space sector.

India welcomed the proposed Summit deliverables on the sustainable use of outer space, accessibility, openness and integrity of space-based scientific data, and support for the International Telecommunication Union’s regulatory framework for frequency management. Dr. Jitendra Singh conveyed India’s readiness to exchange views with the French side during the finalisation of these initiatives.

A key focus of the discussions was India’s contribution to the Paris Summit. Chairman, ISRO/Secretary, Department of Space has been invited to deliver the opening keynote on India’s future human spaceflight in Low Earth Orbit. Dr. Jitendra Singh also conveyed that, if considered useful by the French side, members of the Indian delegation could make presentations on additional areas, including design and manufacturing technologies in space, connectivity from space and exploration beyond the International Space Station.

Prof. Philippe Baptiste expressed France’s desire to further strengthen and accelerate the existing India-France cooperation in space. He also thanked India for the proposed video message from Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the Summit and welcomed continued consultations with the Indian side on the declarations proposed for adoption at the event.

The two sides also discussed France’s participation in the Bengaluru Space Expo and the opportunities for enhanced interaction between the two countries’ space agencies, industries and emerging space ecosystems.

Prof Baptiste is scheduled to visit India from September 28-30, 2026 and has expressed interest in visiting ISRO facilities in Bengaluru and meeting Dr. Jitendra Singh. The two sides agreed that their respective teams would continue consultations on possible areas of cooperation and on the additional presentations proposed for the Paris Summit.

India and France have shared a close space partnership spanning nearly six decades. Cooperation between ISRO and France’s CNES has included the joint satellite missions Megha-Tropiques and SARAL, while the two sides are also pursuing further cooperation in Earth observation and climate-related applications.         

The meeting concluded with both sides reaffirming their commitment to further deepen India-France cooperation in space through innovation, research, human spaceflight, technology development and growing participation of the private space sector.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Felicitates 'Team India School Children' for Historic Best-Ever Performance with 9 Medals in the 19th International Earth Science Olympiad (IESO) 2026
Union Minister for Earth Sciences interacts with and motivates the winning student delegates at Prithvi Bhawan, New Delhi.
India secures its highest-ever medal haul in the history of the event with 4 Gold, 3 Silver, and 2 Bronze medals in Turin, Italy
Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasizes the pivotal role of Ministry-backed youth initiatives in nurturing scientific curiosity and advancing Earth System Science learning.
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 4:26PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today felicitated and interacted with Team India school children, the brilliant young student winners of the 19th International Earth Science Olympiad (IESO) 2026—at a special appreciation and motivation meeting held at Prithvi Bhawan, Lodhi Road, here.

Hailing the extraordinary milestone, Dr Jitendra Singh expressed immense pride in the young achievers, congratulating the winners, their proud parents, and their respective schools for bringing global laurels to the nation. Highlighting the Ministry's vision, the Union Minister noted that the government remains deeply committed to empowering youth through student-centric outreach programs, fostering foundational scientific temperament, and encouraging young minds to explore Earth System Science.

Indian student delegates delivered their best-ever performance at the 19th IESO, held under the aegis of the International Geoscience Organisation in Turin, Italy, from August 20 to 27, 2026. Competing against participants from 39 countries, Team India secured a historic haul of nine medals—comprising 4 Gold, 3 Silver, and 2 Bronze medals—across Written and Practical examinations, International Team Field Investigation (ITFI), and Earth Science Project (ESP) categories.

The stellar medalists who made the country proud include:

Soumik Mandal (DAV Model School, Durgapur, West Bengal): 2 Gold, 1 Silver (Stood 3rd in the overall global ranking among 39 countries)

Aaron Maiti (DAV Model School, IIT-KGP, West Bengal): 1 Gold, 1 Bronze

Riddhi Ranjan (Gyan Asthali International School, Patna, Bihar): 1 Gold, 1 Silver

Md Ehtesham Rizwi Bihar (JNV, Silver 1, Bronze 1

Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), also joined in commending the contingent, praising the students and mentors for recording India’s highest-ever medal tally in the competition's history.

Rigorous National Selection & Training Pipeline preceded the participation in the prestigious Olympiad. The journey to international victory reflects structured national backing. Fully supported by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) under its Outreach and Awareness program, the Earth Science Olympiad begins with an all-India test—facilitated by the Geological Society of India (GSI)—which saw approximately 17,800 students appear across 500 centers nationwide. The top 25 meritorious students underwent an intensive three-week training camp in June 2026 at M.S. University, Vadodara, Gujarat, conducted as desired by the Union Minister to rotate camp locations across different regions of the country.

Through flagship initiatives like the IESO, alongside major national missions such as the Deep Ocean Mission, Mission Mausam, and PRITHVI, the Ministry of Earth Sciences continues to build robust public scientific awareness and inspire the next generation of geoscientists and researchers.

 

 

PHOTO - Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh felicitating 'Team India School Children' for their performance in the 19th International Earth Science Olympiad (IESO) 2026 at Prithvi Bhawan, New Delhi on Friday.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
89th Fit India Sundays on Cycle to Promote PM Modi’s Call for ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya to Lead Cycling Initiative in Surat; Gujarat Deputy CM Harsh Sanghvi to Participate
Padma Shri Olympian Achanta Sharath Kamal, Arjuna Awardee Sarita Mor Among Prominent Sportspersons to Join Initiative
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi

The 89th edition of Fit India Sundays on Cycle will be organised in Surat on September 6, with the theme ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’, promoting fitness, sports and community participation as means to encourage a healthy and drug-free youth.

Union Minister for Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya will lead the cycling initiative, with Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghvi also participating.

“Taking forward Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’, this edition of Fit India Sundays on Cycle is dedicated to encouraging our youth to stay away from drugs and embrace a healthy and active lifestyle. Through Sundays on Cycle and other fitness activities, Fit India is helping build a generation that is healthy, confident and disciplined, and committed to building a Viksit Bharat,” Dr. Mandaviya said.

Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had highlighted drug abuse as a major crisis for the country and its youth.

The 89th edition also aligns with the 100-week nationwide Jan Bhagidari campaign under the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’, which seeks to build a sustained movement against substance abuse through sports, fitness, awareness and community participation.

The cycling event in Surat will begin at 6:00 AM from Sardar Patel Statue, Mangadh Chowk, pass through Mini Bazaar and Varachha Main Road, and culminate at Sarthana Zoo.

Eminent sportspersons including Padma Shri Olympian Achanta Sharath Kamal, Arjuna Awardee Sarita Mor, wrestler Shivani Pawar and Commonwealth medallist Rahul Mann will also participate in the initiative.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President inaugurates Advanced Instrumentation Facility and Tech Innovation Forum at Panjab University, Chandigarh 
Vice President calls for collective efforts to transform Panjab University into a world-class institution 
India emerging as a global destination for quality education and research: Vice President
Vice President urges students to say ‘No to Drugs’ and contribute to building a Nasha Mukt Bharat
Campus safety must be the University’s top priority, says Vice President
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 3:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India and Ex-officio Chancellor of Panjab University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited Panjab University, Chandigarh today.During his visit, the Vice-President inaugurated the Advanced Instrumentation Facility at the Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facility/Central Instrumentation Laboratories (SAIF/CIL). He also inaugurated the Panjab University Tech Innovation Forum (PU-TIF). SAIF/CIL and PU-TIF represent important components of the University's ecosystem for academic, applied and translational research, providing advanced analytical, incubation and entrepreneurial support to researchers, innovators and industry.

The Vice-President of India and Ex-officio Chancellor of Panjab University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited Panjab University, Chandigarh today.

The Vice-President inaugurated the Advanced Instrumentation Facility at the Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facility/Central… pic.twitter.com/SStJVw1YTC

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 4, 2026

Addressing the gathering, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled the University’s distinguished legacy since its establishment in 1882 and noted its contribution to nation-building through generations of leaders, jurists, scientists, sportspersons and public servants.

Vice-President of India and Ex-Officio Chancellor of Panjab University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, inaugurated advanced scientific infrastructure facilities at Panjab University, Chandigarh, today.

He expressed confidence that these facilities and the Panjab University Tech… pic.twitter.com/g42GnrZVKv

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 4, 2026

The Vice-President said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Bharat’s higher education and scientific research ecosystem has undergone a transformative change. He observed that India is increasingly emerging as a global destination for quality education, research and innovation.

Describing the day’s inaugurations as two important milestones, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the installation of five advanced scientific instruments Atomic Force Microscope, Raman Spectrometer, DNA Sequencer, Flow Cytometer and FTIR Spectrometer, would significantly strengthen the University’s research capabilities in fields including nanotechnology, materials science, environmental science and genomics.

Highlighting the importance of innovation, the Vice-President said that the transformation of Bio-NEST into the Panjab University Tech Innovation Forum as a Section 8 not-for-profit company represents a new institutional framework for advancing research, entrepreneurship and technology development. He emphasised that innovation thrives when academia, industry, incubators and investors work together.

Addressing young researchers, he urged them to pursue science with purpose, remain resilient in the face of failure, and develop innovations that are inclusive, scalable and capable of addressing real societal needs. He said that research should have a meaningful impact on society. He called upon researchers and students to pursue research in the right direction so that its benefits reach society at large.

The Vice-President also addressed campus safety, stating that following the unfortunate death of a Ph.D. student, he had immediately directed the University authorities to undertake a comprehensive safety audit of the entire campus. He said an internal committee has been constituted to review the existing infrastructure and submit a detailed report, and stressed that the safety and well-being of students and staff must remain the University’s highest priority.

Calling upon students to contribute towards a “Nasha Mukt Bharat”, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan urged them to stay away from substance abuse and encourage their families and friends to do the same.

Concluding his address, the Vice-President expressed confidence that the advanced scientific facilities and the Panjab University Tech Innovation Forum would further strengthen the University’s contribution to research, innovation and entrepreneurship. He urged students and faculty to ensure that ideas emerging from classrooms and laboratories translate into opportunities for youth and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat and Atmanirbhar Bharat.He called for collective efforts and invited suggestions from the university community on measures to transform Panjab University into a world-class institution of higher education and research.

Governor of Panjab & Administrator Chandigarh U.T., Shri Gulab Chand Kataria; Governor of Haryana, Prof. Ashim Kumar Ghosh; Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, Shri Manish Tiwari; Vice-Chancellor of Panjab University, Professor Meenakshi Goyal and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

***

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Geothermal Energy
A New Chapter in India's Clean Energy Journey
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 2:43PM by PIB Delhi

The intense heat in the Earth's interior is a powerful source of clean energy called geothermal energy. Given India's rich geothermal resources, this form of energy holds immense promise as a round-the-clock available source of power. The National Policy on Geothermal Energy aims to harness this potential. It seeks to make geothermal energy a key part of the nation's renewable energy story as India drives towards Net Zero by 2070. The recent commissioning of the first two geothermal wells in Ladakh marks the beginning of this journey. 

 

Harnessing Geothermal Energy for a Sustainable India

Deep below the Earth's surface, emanating from the intense heat of its interiors, lies a constant, low-carbon source of energy called geothermal energy. In locations with suitable geology and tectonics, this energy can be tapped to generate power or used directly on the ground. Unlike solar and wind energy, this source provides renewable energy that is available round the clock. Recognising this potential, the Government notified the National Policy on Geothermal Energy in September 2025. The policy charts a clear roadmap for exploring and developing India's geothermal resources. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is the nodal ministry for its implementation.

Building on this framework, India achieved a historic milestone in July 2026. The ONGC Energy Centre commissioned the country's first two geothermal wells in Puga Valley, Ladakh. At a height of over 14,000 feet above sea level, Puga Valley is among India's most promising geothermal sites, known for its hot springs and underground heat reserves. The two 1,000-metre-deep wells will support reservoir evaluation. They also pave the way for India's first 1-megawatt demonstration geothermal power project, marking the country's entry into geothermal power generation.

As India advances its clean energy transition, geothermal power offers a dependable, indigenous way to diversify the nation's renewable energy mix.

Understanding Geothermal Energy: An Overview

Geothermal Energy is a steady, low-carbon and weather-independent energy source. It holds a vast untapped resource base to strengthen India's clean energy future and cut reliance on fossil fuels.

Formation of Geothermal Energy

The Earth's interior consists of four main layers: the outermost, solid crust; the middle, semi-solid mantle; and the core divided into a dense liquid outer core and solid inner core. The temperature of the interior rises with depth - the mantle temperature reaches about 3700 Celsius degrees at its boundary with the core, while the core temperature goes up to 5000- 6000 Celsius.  This heat is generated by radioactive decay of elements like uranium, thorium, and potassium, as well as residual heat left over from the planet's formation.  This heat gives rise to huge convection currents in the mantle, as hot material moves up from the core boundary towards the cooler, upper parts of the mantle and crust. This material also contains water trapped as hydroxides.  These convection currents give rise to all tectonic activity, including earthquakes, volcanoes and mountain building. In geologically active regions, faults and fractures let the hot material travel closer to the surface. This process creates reservoirs of hot water and steam, trapped within permeable rock. This thermal energy, harnessed from within the Earth, is known as geothermal energy.

From Geothermal Energy to Power Production

Geothermal power generation converts the earth's natural heat into electricity by tapping hot water and steam trapped beneath the surface. Deep wells bring these resources up to the surface. The steam then drives a turbine connected to a generator. This process resembles conventional thermal power generation. However, it replaces fuel combustion with naturally occurring underground heat. After power generation, the used water is condensed and reinjected into the reservoir. This supports resource replenishment and enables continued energy production. Geothermal energy also supports direct heat applications across district heating, agriculture, aquaculture, and space heating & cooling, enabling efficient utilisation of geothermal heat.

Inside the Earth

From the centre outward, the Earth is structured in four distinct layers. The inner core is a solid ball of iron and nickel, about 2,400 km wide. The outer core surrounding it is a liquid layer of molten iron and nickel, roughly 2,400 km thick. The mantle, composed mostly of hot, dense rock, extends nearly 2,900 km and forms the largest layer. Finally, the crust is the thin, solid outer layer, ranging from about 5 to 8 kilometres thick beneath the oceans to 24 to 56 kilometres thick beneath the continents.

 

India's Geothermal Resource Base

India's varied geology offers a strong foundation for geothermal development. The Geological Survey of India (GSI) has mapped 381 hot springs and identified 10 geothermal provinces nationwide. India's theoretical geothermal prospect stands at nearly 10.6 GW. Of this, 42 sites have been recognised as promising for power generation and direct heat use.

The 10 geothermal provinces include the Himalayan Geothermal Province, Naga-Lusai, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Son Narmada Tapi (SONATA), West Coast, Cambay Graben, Aravalli, Mahanadi, Godavari, and South Indian Cratonic regions.

India's geothermal rift basins hold strong scope, owing to favourable geology and tectonics. But suitable projects can arise anywhere geothermal resources exist. Advanced technologies like Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) and Advanced Geothermal Systems (AGS) will further widen exploration opportunities.

 

Repurposing Abandoned Oil and Gas Wells

Geothermal energy can be extracted from abandoned oil and gas wells. Inactive or unproductive wells can potentially be repurposed for geothermal initiatives, subject to technical and operational feasibility. This approach builds on existing drilling expertise, well data and infrastructure from the oil and gas sector.

 

India’s Geothermal Expansion

India is moving from resource assessment to field demonstration with remarkable speed. This momentum is reflected in the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy sanctioning five research and development projects between July and August 2025, covering resource assessment, indigenous technology development and field demonstration. The projects span electricity generation, heating and cooling applications. These efforts are generating the technical data and field experience needed for future commercial deployment.

 

Project

Current Status of Government-supported Projects

as of 12 December 2026

Ankleshwar, Gujarat

A pilot project evaluating electricity generation by retrofitting unproductive oil and gas wells. Field investigations and baseline geological and production data have been completed.

Gandhinagar, Gujarat

A demonstration project integrating solar and geothermal energy has drilled three geothermal wells that produce geothermal fluid at 70 to 80°C and has demonstrated electricity generation of 50 to 90 kilowatts.

Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh

Studies are underway at five geothermal sites to assess the region's geothermal resource through field investigations and geochemical analysis.

Hyderabad, Telangana

A research project is developing a geothermal cooling system for air conditioning applications using modelling and performance analysis.

Shallow Geothermal Energy

Pilot study is developing analytical models to evaluate shallow geothermal systems using Borehole Heat Exchangers for heating and cooling applications.

 

Significant geothermal resources, advancing technologies and early field activity are laying the foundation for a future of geothermal energy in India. While commercial-scale power generation is yet to be established, expanding well fields, demonstration activities and research and development initiatives are strengthening the ecosystem for wider deployment.

Unlocking India’s Geothermal Potential: Policy & Partnerships

Geothermal energy is a proven, established renewable technology worldwide. Global installed capacity reached 15.67 GW by the end of 2025. Indonesia, the US, the Philippines, Türkiye and New Zealand lead the field, together holding around 67% of global capacity. India is now building a strong ecosystem to advance geothermal energy from resource assessment to real-world deployment. National programmes and international partnerships are driving this mission forward, powering research, technology development and knowledge exchange across the sector.

National Policy on Geothermal Energy, 2025

The National Policy on Geothermal Energy aims to establish geothermal energy as a major renewable pillar. It promotes systematic exploration and deployment of India's geothermal resources. The Policy prioritises research, drilling, reservoir management, and direct-use applications. It also supports Ground Source Heat Pumps (GSHPs) for heating and cooling. A clear regulatory framework encourages both public and private sector participation. The Policy facilitates repurposing abandoned oil and gas wells for geothermal use. It further supports a national geothermal data repository, pilot projects, and Centres of Excellence.

 Renewable Energy Research and Technology Development Programme (RE-RTD)

MNRE is implementing the RE-RTD scheme through research institutions and industry partners. This initiative aims to develop indigenous, cost-effective technologies for renewable energy, including geothermal energy, across the country.

International Collaborations

India has advanced its geothermal energy efforts through collaborations with several international partners. Under cooperation mechanisms with Australia and Iceland, geothermal energy has been identified as a key area of cooperation. Similarly, an MoU with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia designated geothermal energy as a focus area of bilateral engagement.

These initiatives are providing a coordinated platform for translating India’s geothermal resources into scalable solutions across sectors.

New Dimension in India’s Renewable Energy Mix

India's geothermal energy journey reflects the Government's steadfast commitment to energy security and sustainable growth. From notifying the National Policy on Geothermal Energy to commissioning the country's first two geothermal wells at Puga Valley, Ladakh, India has moved decisively from planning to implementation. The country holds a theoretical geothermal resource potential of nearly 10,600 MW. Growing pilot projects and strengthening international collaborations are expanding its applications, from power generation to heating, geo-tourism and agriculture. Geothermal energy is thus emerging as a valuable addition to India's renewable energy portfolio. As India advances towards its 2070 Net Zero target, geothermal energy will remain a steady, indigenous pillar of the country's energy transition and progress.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2,306 long pending pension grievances redressed during Special Campaign 3
72% of targeted grievance cases were redressed by the end of Special Campaign 3
Special Campaign 3 bridges Digital divide with majority redressal from rural areas through CPENGRAMS Portal
Special Campaign 3 reposes faith in governance with redressal of long-pending pension grievances
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 2:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW) is committed towards the welfare of the central government pensioners, including the meaningful and accessible redressal of their grievances. For this, annual special campaigns have been organized since 2024. In the third edition, the department started Special Campaign 3 on 7th July, 2026, for the timely and qualitative redressal of long-pending pension grievances/claims/issues. This campaign had a preparatory phase and an execution phase and concluded on 31st August, 2026.

During the preparatory phase, all ministries, departments, and their attached or subordinate offices were mandated to identify long-pending grievances, claims, and issues received via both online and physical modes. Ministries and departments identified 1,062 target cases under this phase. Further, 2,131 grievance cases pending on the CPENGRAMS portal for more than one month were also taken for redressal in this phase.

During the execution phase, the department actively coordinated with the ministries/department for redressal of these cases. Two mid-campaign review meetings were held, and the status of the pendency of these cases was sought regularly.

Coordinated efforts of 40 ministries/departments have culminated in the successful resolution of 2,306 cases out of 3,193 taken-up cases, registering the redressal rate of 72%. Active follow-up is being done for the redressal of remaining grievances.

The demographic distribution of the redressal reflects that most of the resolved cases pertain to the pensioners and family pensioners residing in rural areas. It is a healthy trend, as the redirection of grievances from rural areas in online mode through various portals operated by ministries/departments and CPENGRAMS portal, is bridging the digital divide.

The collective efforts have resulted in the successful redressal of some long-pending cases.

Some major success cases are:

1. Release of Rs. 16.70 lakh on account of family pension arrears to Ms. Jayalakshmi Karnan, the disabled dependent daughter of a Defence pensioner, with effect from June, 2013.

2. Settlement of disability pension arrears of Rs. 30 lakh in favour of Shri Idan Singh, a Defence pensioner, with effect from 16.09.2016

3. Sh. Kapur Singh, a defense pensioner, received Rs. 26.12 lakh as war injury element arrears, with effect from 01.01.2006.

4. Release of dual family pension arrears amounting to Rs. 19 Lakh, with effect from 24.09.2012, in favour of Ms. Rukmani Nair, spouse of a Defence pensioner.

5. Payment of outstanding Special family pension arrears along with interest amounting to Rs. 18.57 lakh and arrear of Ex gratia along with interest amounting to Rs. 12.60 lakh to Ms. Saranjit Kaur, mother of an army personnel with effect from 28.07.2008.

6. Release of pending family pension arrears of Rs. 6.27 lakh to Ms. Sunaina Kumari, widow daughter of a Defence pensioner, with effect from 18.03.2022.

7. A payment of Rs. 10.66 lakh towards arrears of the liberalized family pension was paid to Ms. Simarto, spouse of a Defence pensioner, with effect from 01.01.1996.

8. Disbursement of family pension arrears of Rs. 37.40 lakh to Ms. Angoori Devi, spouse of a Defence pensioner, towards difference between Ordinary Family Pension and Special Family pension, with effect from 01.01.1996.

9. Disbursement of Rs. 25.99 lakh towards the time-barred arrears of service pension arrears to Sh. Ranjit Singh, a Defence pensioner, pertaining to the period from October, 2004, to December, 2023.

10. Payment of Rs. 30.15 lakh to Ms. Koranga Lakshmi, spouse of a Defence pensioner, towards family pension arrears from June, 2011, to February, 2026.

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister congratulates Italian PM Giorgia Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 1:07PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today congratulated Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history.

The Prime Minister stated that this milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership. He further noted that her friendship has been instrumental in strengthening the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership, adding that he looks forward to continuing their close cooperation to build a prosperous future for the people of both countries. He extended his best wishes for her continued success in the years ahead.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared:

"Congratulations to my friend Prime Minister Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history. This milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership.

Her friendship has also been instrumental in strengthening the India-Italy Special Strategic
Partnership and I look forward to continuing our close cooperation to build a prosperous future for the people of our countries.

My best wishes for her continued success in the years ahead.

@GiorgiaMeloni"

NCPCR undertook coordinated measures with the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations, District Magistrates, Labour Departments, Police authorities and other…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
NCPCR rescues over 3800 Children from Child Labour under a special Campaign
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 11:04AM by PIB Delhi

National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), a statutory body under Ministry of Women and Child Development launched a special “Pan-India Rescue and Rehabilitation” Campaign on 12 June 2026, which continued up to 31 August 2026. NCPCR undertook coordinated measures with the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations, District Magistrates, Labour Departments, Police authorities and other stakeholders to intensify the identification, rescue and rehabilitation of children engaged in child labour and those vulnerable to trafficking and exploitation.

The NCPCR issued communications to the concerned authorities requesting intensified and targeted rescue operations at child labour and trafficking hotspots.States/UTs were also requested to furnish regular data on rescue operations, children rescued, FIRs registered, rehabilitation, restoration, educational mainstreaming, compensation and other follow-up measures etc.

To monitor implementation and address field level issues, the NCPCR conducted meetings with the District Administrations. The meetings focused on reviewing rescue operations, addressing operational bottlenecks, ensuring timely submission of ATRs and strengthening coordination among the concerned Departments and agencies.

The NCPCR also undertook awareness and outreach through social media and other communication platforms, disseminating information regarding the campaign, reporting of child labour and the importance of rehabilitation and educational mainstreaming following rescue.

With sustained and proactive monitoring of above campaign, NCPCR in collaboration with State authorities successfully rescued over 3,800 children. Further, over 575 FIRs have been registered during the Campaign.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today hailed yet another outstanding achievement by ISRO, calling it a proud moment for the nation.

The Prime Minister stated that the successful launch of GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous orbit, is a reflection of the excellence, innovation, and growing capabilities that define India’s space sector.

Shri Modi further noted that the growing partnership between ISRO and the Indian industry is adding new strength and scale to the space programme, expanding India’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared:

"Yet another outstanding achievement by ISRO and a proud moment for our nation.

The successful launch of GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous orbit is a reflection of the excellence, innovation and growing capabilities that define India’s space sector.
The growing partnership between ISRO and Indian industry is adding new strength and scale to our space programme and expanding India’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem."

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Union Minister Shri Ramdas Athawale Inaugurates Distribution of NAMASTE Cards to Waste Pickers in MCD Najafgarh Zone; Ayushman Cards Also Distributed Among Beneficiaries at New Delhi Event Union Minister Lauds untiring contribution of waste pickers in Nation’s Sanitation & Hygiene; Assures Government's full cooperation and continued support in improving their working conditions and access to welfare schemes Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 9:02AM by PIB Delhi Shri Ramdas Athawale, Union Minister of State for Social Justice and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Shri Ramdas Athawale Inaugurates Distribution of NAMASTE Cards to Waste Pickers in MCD Najafgarh Zone; Ayushman Cards Also Distributed Among Beneficiaries at New Delhi Event
Union Minister Lauds untiring contribution of waste pickers in Nation’s Sanitation & Hygiene; Assures Government's full cooperation and continued support in improving their working conditions and access to welfare schemes
Posted On: 04 SEP 2026 9:02AM by PIB Delhi

Shri Ramdas Athawale, Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, inaugurated the issuance of NAMASTE Cards to waste pickers of the MCD Najafgarh Zone at a programme held at the MCD Community Hall, Matiala, in the National Capital.

The event marked a significant step in the formal recognition and empowerment of waste pickers under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) scheme, aimed at improving the safety, dignity, and socio-economic status of sanitation workers across the country.

Alongside the NAMASTE Cards, the Minister also distributed Ayushman Cards among the waste pickers present, extending healthcare coverage benefits to this vital workforce.

In his address, Shri Athawale lauded the tireless contribution of waste pickers in keeping Indian cities clean, describing their work as essential to the nation's sanitation and public health efforts. He assured the workers of the Government's full cooperation and continued support in improving their working conditions and access to welfare schemes.

Shri Ramdas Athawale addressing the gathering at the event

More than 300 waste pickers from the Najafgarh Zone participated in the programme.

The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, implemented to ensure the safety, dignity, and socio-economic upliftment of sanitation workers, including sewer and septic tank workers and waste pickers. The scheme focuses on occupational safety, formal recognition of workers, access to healthcare and social security benefits, skill development, and mechanisation of hazardous sanitation work, with the aim of eliminating hazardous manual cleaning practices across the country.

item.title: Ministry of Tribal Affairs Reviews Progress of PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA; Announces Key Initiatives for Strengthening Tribal Development
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Tribal Affairs Ministry of Tribal Affairs Reviews Progress of PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA; Announces Key Initiatives for Strengthening Tribal Development ITDA Roadmap and Operational Guidelines, Adi Darpan and District Agri DPR Challenge Awardees Announced; National Conclave on Tribal Women Entrepreneurs to Advance Women-Led Economic Empowerment Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 11:17PM by PIB Delhi Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secy, MoTA reviews Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ schemes such as DAJGUA and PM JANMAN on 3rd September 2026 with a focus on strengthening delivery…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Ministry of Tribal Affairs Reviews Progress of PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA; Announces Key Initiatives for Strengthening Tribal Development
ITDA Roadmap and Operational Guidelines, Adi Darpan and District Agri DPR Challenge Awardees Announced; National Conclave on Tribal Women Entrepreneurs to Advance Women-Led Economic Empowerment
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 11:17PM by PIB Delhi

Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secy, MoTA reviews Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ schemes such as DAJGUA and PM JANMAN on 3rd September 2026 with a focus on strengthening delivery mechanisms, improving convergence, accelerating fund utilisation and addressing implementation bottlenecks across states and implementing agencies.

The review, held under the Chairpersonship of Smt. Ranjana Chopra,Secretary Ministry of Tribal Affairs brought together senior officials of the Ministry INCLUDING Additional Secretary Manish Thakur and other senior officers, the National Programme Management Unit (NPMU), State Governments and implementing agencies to assess the physical and financial progress of key interventions and deliberate on measures to enhance their effectiveness and impact. The meeting included a detailed component-wise review of the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA).

Key Announcements and Their Developmental Impact

1. Strengthening ITDA Governance and Decentralised Planning : The Roadmap for Integrated Tribal Development Agencies/Projects (ITDAs/ITDPs) along with comprehensive ITDA Operational Guidelines was shared with the states and ministries. The documents establish a structured framework for planning, governance and monitoring of ITDAs/ITDPs, with the objective of strengthening institutional mechanisms and facilitating greater convergence of Central and State interventions at the district and block levels. The framework is expected to support more effective decentralised planning, improve fund utilisation, minimise implementation delays and facilitate the adoption of replicable models for tribal development across States.

2. Release of Adi Darpan:  The Adi Darpan - a comprehensive compendium reflecting the progress of the Ministry's schemes and programmes as well as the ground realities and development profile of tribal communities across the country was also released at the Consultative meeting. Conceived as a ready reference on tribal development, Adi Darpan is intended to strengthen transparency, facilitate evidence-based planning and provide policymakers, researchers and citizens with greater visibility into the implementation and outcomes of tribal development interventions.

3. District Agri DPR Challenge: The winning districts of the District Agri Detailed Project Report (DPR) Challenge were announced. The Challenge invited districts to develop high-quality, implementation-ready DPRs for agriculture and allied livelihood interventions benefiting tribal farmers.The initiative seeks to promote innovation and strengthen the quality of agri-livelihood planning, particularly in areas such as horticulture, water management and value-chain development. Recognition of well-designed DPRs is intended to encourage replicable models and facilitate the deployment of DA-JGUA resources towards planned, high-impact interventions capable of contributing to sustainable improvements in farm incomes in tribal areas. Winners included - Wayanad, Dima Hasao, Palghar and Palakkad across Kerala, Assam and Maharashtra

4. National Conclave on Tribal Women Entrepreneurs:  The upcoming Rani Durgavati Adivasi Mahila Sammelan – National Conclave on Tribal Women Entrepreneurs was also presented during the meeting by Dr Varnali Deka, Director DAJGUA. Named in honour of the celebrated tribal warrior-queen Rani Durgavati, the national conclave is envisaged as a platform to strengthen opportunities for tribal women entrepreneurs through market linkages, access to credit, skilling and mentorship. The initiative reflects the Ministry's continued emphasis on enabling women-led enterprises, promoting economic self-reliance and strengthening Nari Shakti in tribal regions.

Comprehensive Review of Scheme Implementation

The review examined the component-wise progress of PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA, including physical and financial achievements, convergence with line ministries and key implementation challenges. Particular attention was given to the status of Utilisation Certificates (UCs) and expenditure commitments under DA-JGUA, PM-JANMAN and Article 275(1), with emphasis on expediting fund utilisation during the remaining period of the financial year.

Progress of the TMMC initiative, the Centre of Competence for Sickle Cell Disease and the CSIR-NBRI bioresource initiative was also reviewed. These initiatives underscore the Ministry's efforts to strengthen health-related interventions for tribal communities while harnessing traditional knowledge and bioresources for developmental outcomes.

The meeting further reviewed the implementation of the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan, including registrations at Adi Sewa Kendras and enrolment of Adi Karmayogi Volunteers. A demonstration of the iGoT microsite developed for capacity-building of volunteers was also undertaken, reinforcing the focus on developing a trained, responsive and service-oriented grassroots cadre.

The review concluded with the identification of specific action points to strengthen implementation, improve coordination among stakeholders and accelerate the delivery of outcomes under the Ministry's flagship interventions. The exercise reaffirmed the Ministry's commitment to ensuring effective, accountable and outcome-oriented tribal development in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Convenes National Workshop on “SUMAN Roadmap 2030 – Accelerating the Continuum of Care”
Registration of Newly Married Couples Can Help Prevent Unintended Pregnancies and Enable Healthy, Planned Pregnancies: Shri Brajesh Pathak, Deputy Chief Minister, Government of Uttar Pradesh.
SUMAN Roadmap 2030 to Strengthen Continuum of Maternal and Newborn Care, with Focus on Vulnerable and Underserved Areas: Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NHM
Workshop Focused on Translating SUMAN Roadmap 2030 from Vision to Action towards Zero Preventable Maternal and Newborn Deaths.
SUMAN Roadmap 2030 Focuses on 13 High-Focus States and 130 Districts with Targeted Strategies to Reduce Maternal and Newborn Deaths
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 11:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) convened a two-day National Workshop on “SUMAN Roadmap 2030 – Accelerating the Continuum of Care” on September 2–3, 2026 at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.

The workshop was held under the chairpersonship of Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. The inaugural session was attended by Shri Brajesh Pathak, Deputy Chief Minister and Minister of Medical Education, Medical Health, Family Welfare, Mother & Child Welfare, Government of Uttar Pradesh.

Addressing the inaugural session, Shri Brajesh Pathak highlighted the importance of registration of newly married couples as an important step towards preventing unintended pregnancies and enabling timely preparation for healthy and planned pregnancies. He reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of Uttar Pradesh towards effective implementation of the SUMAN Roadmap 2030 across the State, with a focus on ensuring safe, respectful and quality maternal and newborn healthcare for every woman and newborn.

Delivering the keynote address, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NHM, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, highlighted that, “India has made substantial progress in reducing maternal mortality and that sustained and targeted efforts are being undertaken to accelerate further gains, particularly in high-MMR States and vulnerable and hard-to-reach areas”.

She also emphasised that maternal health lies at the core of the health system’s efforts for women and families. Underscoring that pregnancy is a physiological process associated with joy and hope for families, she stressed the importance of ensuring that every woman experience pregnancy and childbirth with safety, dignity and access to quality care.

Smt. Patnaik highlighted that the SUMAN Roadmap 2030 adopts a life-course and continuum-of-care approach, integrating interventions across the entire maternal health journey—from pre-pregnancy care and antenatal care to intrapartum and postnatal care. The roadmap provides a focused and multidimensional framework to address critical gaps, strengthen existing health systems and ensure timely, equitable and quality maternal and newborn healthcare, with particular attention to vulnerable populations and underserved geographies.

During the inaugural session, the Guidelines on Birth Waiting Home (BWH), IEC material on SUMAN Roadmap 2030 and a video on SUMAN Roadmap 2030 were also launched, further strengthening the resources available for effective implementation of the roadmap at the State and field levels.

The workshop brought together more than 200 participants from across the country, including Mission Directors and senior officials from States and Union Territories, representatives from Central and State Governments, technical experts, academic institutions, professional bodies and development partners. The diverse participation facilitated cross-learning, exchange of field experiences and focused deliberations on State-specific priorities for accelerating progress under the SUMAN Roadmap 2030.

The SUMAN Roadmap 2030 adopts a two-part approach to address the specific needs of States and districts while ensuring sustained progress across the country. Section A focuses on targeted strategies for 13 High-Focus States and 130 districts that account for a disproportionate share of maternal and newborn deaths. Section B outlines strategies for all States and Union Territories to achieve and sustain progress towards the Sustainable Development Goal targets.

Building on this framework, the technical sessions focused on critical interventions across the continuum of maternal and newborn care. Discussions covered Pre-Pregnancy Care; High-Risk Pregnancy and management of Post-Partum Haemorrhage (PPH); community-level focused interventions; optimisation of Caesarean Section services; the role of the private sector in strengthening maternal health services; digital health initiatives; SUMAN Call Centre and grievance redressal mechanism; operationalisation of Birth Waiting Homes; and the impact of climate change on maternal health.

A key component of the workshop was the presentation by the 13 High-Focus States, which shared their respective priorities, key implementation gaps and proposed actions under the SUMAN Roadmap 2030. The session enabled States to learn from one another’s experiences and identify context-specific and actionable strategies to accelerate improvements in maternal and newborn health outcomes.

The workshop also provided a platform for showcasing promising State-level innovations and field experiences through a Gallery Walk. The initiatives showcased included effective management of PPH using NASG, UBT and drapes by Odisha; SUMAN Panchayat and SUMAN Sakhi Chatbot by Madhya Pradesh; Mothers’ Picnic and Gosaiya Sammelan by Chhattisgarh; State Maternal Health War Room by Uttarakhand; Vatsalya Initiative by Maharashtra; Mission Zero Preventable Maternal Deaths by Karnataka; and digital innovation initiatives by Uttar Pradesh.

Recognising the importance of partnerships in advancing maternal and newborn health, representatives from WHO, UNFPA, UNICEF, Gates Foundation, Jhpiego, FOGSI, C3 and CIFF participated in the deliberations and reaffirmed their commitment to supporting the implementation of the SUMAN Roadmap 2030. Discussions underscored the need for coordinated action, continued technical support and sustained collaboration with development and technical partners to translate the roadmap’s priorities into effective interventions at the field level.

The workshop further adopted an interactive and solution-oriented approach through group exercises on four priority areas—Effective High-Risk Pregnancy Management: Issues and Challenges; Pre-Pregnancy Care: Strategies for Effective Implementation; PPH Management and addressing delays through effective referral transport; and Optimising Caesarean Section Services: Field Experiences. The exercises enabled participants to share practical experiences, identify implementation bottlenecks and develop field-level solutions for strengthening maternal healthcare delivery across States.

The two-day deliberations thus provided a common platform for States, technical experts, academic institutions, professional bodies and development partners to align priorities, share innovations and identify actionable strategies for accelerating the implementation of the SUMAN Roadmap 2030 and advancing the national commitment towards zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths by 2030.

SUMAN Roadmap 2030

The SUMAN Roadmap 2030 provides a strategic framework for accelerating the country’s journey towards zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths by 2030 through high-impact interventions while sustaining progress towards the Sustainable Development Goal targets.

The two-day workshop brought together deliberations across the continuum of maternal health, with focus on Pre-Pregnancy Care, High-Risk Pregnancy, PPH management, third-trimester community-level interventions, optimisation of Caesarean Sections, digital health initiatives, Birth Waiting Homes, climate impact on maternal health, State priorities and partner engagement.

The deliberations reaffirmed the shared national resolve that no woman or newborn should lose their life to a preventable cause. The Ministry reiterated its commitment to working closely with State Governments, technical institutions and development partners to translate the SUMAN Roadmap 2030 into measurable and sustained improvements in maternal and newborn health outcomes, bringing the country closer to the goal of zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths by 2030.

***

SR

item.content:encoded:
Election Commission
“ELCs will empower the Youth to uphold Truth and Strengthen Democracy”: CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 9:20PM by PIB Delhi
  1. The Election Commission of India (ECI) organised its fourth regional conference on "Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC 2.0) and ECINet" in Goa today, focusing on strengthening electoral literacy and democratic awareness among young citizens. Addressing the gathering, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar said that the students are the future of India. He added that Electoral Literacy Clubs across India will help strengthen the world's largest democracy.
  2. Addressing the students and teachers from schools, colleges and universities across Goa, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar stated that ELCs are important platforms for students to understand electoral processes and democratic values.
  3. The Chief Election Commissioner also underlined that elections in India are held strictly as per the Constitution of India, law and instructions issued by ECI and are conducted transparently under the concurrent audit of recognised political parties, candidates or their representatives at all stages.
  4. CEC also highlighted ECINet as the vehicle of transparency for electors across the country, providing a unified digital platform for election-related services and information.
  5. ELC 2.0, with the tagline "Learn Democracy. Lead Democracy.", reimagines Electoral Literacy Clubs as structured, visible and digitally enabled platforms across schools, colleges and universities, encouraging young and first-time voters to understand and meaningfully participate in democracy. Leveraging the extensive ECINet digital platform, which provides all election-related services from roll to poll, the initiative will drive continuous, year-round electoral literacy activities through a dedicated ELC portal, building a streamlined pan-India network of ELCs.
  6. The initiative assumes significance in view of India’s extensive educational ecosystem, comprising approximately 15 lakh schools with nearly 25 crore students and over one crore teachers. The higher education sector comprises nearly 1,500 universities and around 70,000 educational institutions, with an estimated enrolment of 4.33 crore students.
  7. Through this extensive institutional network, ELC 2.0 seeks to promote factual and experiential electoral education, enhance awareness of India’s electoral system, and encourage young citizens to become ambassadors of informed democratic participation. The ELCs will also disseminate information on electoral registration, polling, counting, ECINet App and other key ECI initiatives.
  8. CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar was on a two-day visit to Goa to interact with Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and ELC members from across the State. Yesterday, during an interactive session with over 1,000 BLOs, he commended their dedicated service and contribution to the smooth conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the Electoral Rolls in the State.
  9. The students also had a Question-and-Answer session with the CEC as part of the meeting.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
GeM and Textiles Committee Sign MoU to Boost Procurement of Recycled and Upcycled Textiles
GeM Initiative to Turn Textile Waste into Value-Added Products for Government Buyers
Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 8:57PM by PIB Delhi

Government e Marketplace (GeM), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, and the Textiles Committee (TC), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, have joined hands to promote recycled and upcycled products made from pre- and post-consumer textile waste, scrap and second-hand clothes through public procurement, creating new market opportunities for enterprises in the circular textile economy. The partnership was formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed during the 62nd Foundation Day celebrations of the Textiles Committee in Mumbai.

The collaboration will create a ‘Waste-to-Value-to-Market’ ecosystem, enabling textile waste, scrap and second-hand clothes to be transformed into quality value-added products and made available to Government buyers through GeM.

Under the MoU, the Textiles Committee will identify, verify, certify and recognise eligible producers of recycled and upcycled textile products, besides supporting stakeholder consultations, capacity building, market research and development of technical specifications.

GeM will create dedicated categories for recycled and upcycled textile products, facilitate seller onboarding and online market linkages, and promote these products among Government buyers. Training and handholding support will enable last-mile upcyclers and recyclers to participate effectively in public procurement.

The partnership will follow a hub-and-spoke approach, with the Textiles Committee and its affiliate offices facilitating last-mile outreach, mobilisation and capacity building of upcyclers and recyclers, while supporting the development of appropriate product specifications and catalogues for Government procurement.

With a focus on women, MSMEs, local enterprises, artisans, recyclers and other circular-economy enterprises, the initiative seeks to build an inclusive, decentralised and sustainable production ecosystem, aligned with the national priorities of Vocal for Local, Make in India and AatmaNirbhar Bharat.

The event was graced by the presence of Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, and Minister of Textiles, Government of Maharashtra, Shri Sanjay Savkare. The MoU was signed by Additional CEO, GeM, Shri Ajit B. Chavan, and Secretary, Textiles Committee, Shri Kartikay Dhanda, in the presence of senior officials and industry stakeholders.

Speaking about this significant milestone, CEO (GeM), Shri Mihir Kumar, said “by connecting certification, standardisation and market access, the GeM -TC partnership seeks to create reliable demand for products made from textile waste. Government procurement, with its scale and reach, can accelerate adoption of such products across offices, institutions, gifting and other public-use requirements.”

The initiative will contribute to resource conservation, sustainable livelihoods and responsible consumption and production, while strengthening India’s transition towards a circular and resource-efficient textile economy.

The partnership marks a significant step towards turning textile waste into economic opportunity and sustainable market growth through the scale of public procurement.

***

Abhishek Dayal/Garima Singh/Anushka Pandey
